articles.title: Ricky Rubio: "No volví sólo para jugar, sino para dejar un legado"
articles.standfirst: La estrella del Joventut desvela la motivación que le lleva a seguir jugando con su equipo
articles.summary: La estrella del Joventut desvela la motivación que le lleva a seguir jugando con su equipo
articles.body: El base catalán del Asisa Joventut Ricky Rubio aseguró este martes que regresó al conjunto verdinegro no solo para volver a jugar al baloncesto, sino también con la intención de "dejar un legado" en el club en el que empezó su carrera con 14 años y al que volvió en 2025. "Yo no volví aquí solamente para jugar al baloncesto, sino también para dejar un legado en la ciudad y en el club. Tengo ganas de que este proyecto siga adelante. Hay aspectos que podemos mejorar y quiero que todos tengamos esa ambición para que este club vuelva donde se merece", afirmó el jugador del Masnou (Barcelona). Durante la jornada de atención a los medios previa a la Lliga Catalana, Rubio admitió que el Joventut afronta el nuevo curso con el reto de mantener el nivel alcanzado la pasada temporada: "El año pasado se alcanzaron objetivos muy altos y compararlos con esta temporada es difícil. No hemos podido retener a jugadores que nos habría gustado que continuaran porque tenemos el presupuesto que tenemos", explicó. . Uno de los grandes alicientes del nuevo proyecto será el regreso de Nico Laprovittola al Joventut: "Como aficionado, es un placer y tengo muchas ganas de ver su magia. Creo que es un jugador que ha dado muchísimo a este club en un momento muy delicado y que se le tiene mucho aprecio. Como compañero, ahora podemos compaginarnos mucho más, en una etapa de nuestras carreras en la que puede ser clave que nos ayudemos el uno al otro", destacó. Rubio también explicó los motivos que le llevaron a prolongar una temporada más su etapa en Badalona después de un curso especialmente exigente: "Cuando acabé la temporada pasada terminé físicamente y mentalmente al límite. Cuando acabas de esa manera significa que te lo has dejado todo. Necesité un par de semanas, pero después ya tenía bastante claro que quería volver al proyecto", relató. Dani Miret, entrenador del Joventut, se congratula de poder disponer de dos bases tan determinantes: "Tenemos jugadores que son maestros en el control del partido. Tienes a Ricky, tienes a Nico. Habrá momentos en los que nos interese correr más y otros en los que nos interese correr menos", apuntó.

articles.title: "He venido para liderar al Barça y traer títulos"
articles.standfirst: Justin Robinson, encargado de dirigir la orquesta azulgrana, se pone el listón por las nubes
articles.summary: Justin Robinson, encargado de dirigir la orquesta azulgrana, se pone el listón por las nubes
articles.body: El base Justin Robinson, uno de los once fichajes del Barça, ha asegurado este martes en declaraciones a EFE que se ve preparado para "liderar" el nuevo proyecto azulgrana en una temporada que, espera, sea su "confirmación" como uno de los mejores jugadores de la Euroliga, tras despuntar el curso pasado en París, donde promedió 14,6 puntos y 4,5 asistencias por partido. "El año pasado demostré en la Euroliga de lo que soy capaz y este curso quiero confirmarlo. No creo que recibiera el crédito suficiente por los números que hice y en la situación en la que lo logré, porque el equipo no ganaba demasiado, pero soy un jugador ganador. He ganado siempre durante mi carrera y espero traer eso a Barcelona. No soy perfecto, he tenido muchos altibajos en mi carrera, pero espero poder mostrar mi mejor versión", señala el jugador estadounidense. Asimismo, Robinson, base de 28 años y 1,85 metros nacido en Manassas (Virginia), afirma que tiene "mucho margen de mejora" y, en este sentido, se fija el reto de "ser más consistente en defensa" y recuperar un porcentaje de acierto en triples cercano al 40%. Aunque admite que en los últimos dos años se le etiquetó como "un base anotador", remarca que siempre se vio a sí mismo como un director de juego tradicional: "Me gusta dar asistencias y hacer que sucedan cosas fantasiosas. Hago lo que sea necesario para ganar, me considero un buen compañero y puedo anotar si es necesario". El estadounidense confiesa que tuvo un verano "un poco agitado", pues tras terminar contrato en París fueron "muchos" los equipos que le contactaron y, de hecho, estuvo cerca de firmar con otro, antes de recibir la llamada del equipo azulgrana. "Cuando apareció el Barça pensé que la situación era perfecta. La ACB es una liga fantástica y querían que fuera el base del proyecto. No pude rechazarlo. Estoy muy agradecido por la oportunidad", remarca Robinson, quien se considera un jugador "totalmente diferente" al que llegó al Río Breogán en 2024, debido a su actual "madurez física y mental, experiencia, confianza y conocimiento del juego". Por ello, cree que era "el momento adecuado" para dar este paso y, aunque admite que el Barça necesitará tiempo para funcionar colectivamente tras la llegada de once fichajes -cuatro sin experiencia en Europa- y un entrenador nuevo, confía en que existe "el grupo y el estilo de juego necesarios para superar los altibajos de la temporada y alcanzar la tierra prometida". Sobre la filosofía del técnico Aleksander Sekulic, de quien espera ser su "extensión sobre la pista", expone que el Barça será "muy distinto" al del año pasado: "Vamos a correr, defender duro, tratar de dominar el rebote defensivo y subir el ritmo. Queremos jugar con energía y emocionar al público". Además, comenta que los cuatro jugadores que siguen del año pasado han transmitido a los nuevos "las expectativas de jugar en un club como este, la exposición que da y la enorme responsabilidad que conlleva, la idea de intentar ganarlo todo". Robinson apunta que su objetivo es quedarse en el Barça el resto de su carrera y añade que haber firmado un contrato hasta 2028 le da "seguridad" para afrontar con "tranquilidad" el reto de "ser el líder del equipo y ganar partidos". "Puede que haya dudas sobre si soy el base adecuado, pero voy a demostrar que sí. Quiero empujar al equipo en los momentos difíciles y, en este año de confirmación personal, traer títulos al Palau después de algunas temporadas sería un gran logro", concluye.

articles.title: El palo de Laprovittola al Barça: "Otros invierten más y eso se nota..."
articles.standfirst: El base argentino regresa al Joventut siete años después y firma hasta 2029 · Compartirá vestuario con Ricky Rubio y Ante Tomic · “Fui muy feliz aquí y hoy el club está en unas condiciones bárbaras”
articles.summary: El base argentino regresa al Joventut siete años después y firma hasta 2029 · Compartirá vestuario con Ricky Rubio y Ante Tomic · “Fui muy feliz aquí y hoy el club está en unas condiciones bárbaras”
articles.body: Nicolás Laprovittola vuelve a casa. Siete años después de abandonar Badalona, el base argentino regresa al Joventut con 36 años y con la ilusión intacta. El internacional argentino ha firmado hasta 2029 y afronta una nueva etapa en un club que considera especial y en el que quiere volver a disfrutar del baloncesto. “Dicen que uno vuelve donde ha sido feliz y coincido mucho con esa frase. Fui muy feliz aquí”, reconoció Laprovittola en declaraciones a Radio MARCA. El jugador se mostró encantado con lo que se ha encontrado a su regreso: “Hoy el club está en unas condiciones bárbaras, están cuidando mucho a los jugadores y, sobre todo, a los veteranos. Para mí, en este momento de mi carrera, eso también era importante”. El nuevo proyecto verdinegro ha sido uno de los grandes motivos para regresar. Laprovittola explicó que antes de cerrar su fichaje mantuvo una conversación con el director deportivo, Dani Miret, y con Ricky Rubio. “Ahí me di cuenta de la línea que seguía el equipo, de realmente qué es lo que querían. Hay aspiraciones, hay objetivos y jugamos para ganar. Eso para mí era muy importante”, explicó. Y los objetivos son ambiciosos. El argentino no esconde que el Joventut quiere volver a codearse con los grandes y pelear por títulos. “Estaría muy bueno poder estar en la Copa, creo que ese es un objetivo claro que tenemos”, aseguró. También mira hacia la Supercopa, que el equipo disputará en casa: “Ojalá podamos darle una alegría a la gente”. La ambición alcanza también a la Basketball Champions League: “Hay muchas cosas por jugar, por intentar ganar. Tenemos que trabajar para eso y tenemos que intentar que el Olímpic esté lleno todos los fines de semana”. Laprovittola también echó la vista atrás para hablar de sus últimos años en el Barcelona, una etapa en la que vivió momentos complicados, especialmente por las lesiones y por la dificultad del equipo azulgrana para alcanzar los grandes objetivos europeos. Su análisis fue sincero: “Me hubiese gustado crecer ganando, pero el escenario no era fácil”. El argentino puso en contexto las dificultades que atravesó el Barça durante ese periodo y señaló la diferencia de inversión respecto a otros grandes clubes europeos. “Hay otros equipos en Europa que aspiran a ganar, que invierten muchísimo más que lo que invirtió el Barça y eso al final se nota”, explicó. A pesar de todo, Laprovittola se queda con una etapa muy importante de su carrera y con el cariño recibido en Barcelona. Superó los 300 partidos con el conjunto azulgrana, aunque las lesiones marcaron parte de sus últimos años, incluida una grave lesión de rodilla. Ahora, ya lejos del Palau, prefiere mirar hacia adelante: “Hay que pensar en el futuro”. “Esperemos que este año haya pasado todo lo malo y podamos disfrutar mucho. Soy una persona bastante positiva. Creo que todavía me queda mucho más por jugar”, aseguró el base, que quiere dejar atrás definitivamente los problemas físicos y disfrutar de su regreso a Badalona. En su regreso se reencontrará además con Ricky Rubio, con quien ya compartió vestuario en el pasado. El vínculo entre ambos tiene incluso una curiosa historia: cuando Laprovittola jugaba en Utah Jazz, Rubio apareció en una rueda de prensa con la camiseta del argentino del Joventut. Ahora serán compañeros otra vez. “Hoy en día estamos compartiendo equipo, así que estoy muy contento de tener a Ricky de compañero otra vez. Ojalá podamos estar muchos minutos en cancha y tengamos una muy buena conexión”, señaló. El argentino también quiere asumir un papel importante dentro del vestuario. Junto a Ricky Rubio, Ante Tomic y otros jugadores experimentados, será uno de los referentes de un equipo que pretende mezclar veteranía y juventud. “Voy a cuidar mucho de mis compañeros. Creo que, como capitán, Ricky también es un referente. Voy a estar ahí para apoyarlos en todo”, afirmó, aunque rechazó con humor el papel de “padre” de los jóvenes: “No, no, papá soy de mi casa”. La vuelta a Badalona tiene además un componente sentimental. Para Laprovittola, la identidad del Joventut está estrechamente ligada a la ciudad. “La Peña, la ciudad de Badalona, son lugares donde se respira básquet. Uno va a tomarse un café y habla del básquet, no se habla de otra cosa”, explicó. “Ver a los chicos con un balón en la calle son cosas que no hay en otro lugar”. Ahora quiere devolver ese cariño sobre la pista. Después de unos últimos años complicados en Barcelona, Laprovittola mira hacia adelante con optimismo. Y también mantiene vivo otro sueño: volver a disputar un Mundial con Argentina. “Primero tenemos que clasificar, pero después creo que sería algo muy lindo para mí poder jugar otro Mundial con Argentina”, confesó. Laprovittola vuelve a Badalona. Lo hace siete años después, con más experiencia, con una familia y con un currículum mucho más amplio. Pero con la misma esencia. La Peña recupera a uno de los jugadores que más huella dejó en su primera etapa y él regresa al lugar donde, como reconoce, fue feliz.

articles.title: El exbaskonista Omoruyi se lía a puñetazos contra el CSKA
articles.standfirst: El alero nigeriano del Besiktas inició la pelea del amistoso al dar un bofetón al ruso Ukhov
articles.summary: El alero nigeriano del Besiktas inició la pelea del amistoso al dar un bofetón al ruso Ukhov
articles.body: El exbaskonista Eugene Omoruyi protagonizó el episodio más caliente del amistoso entre el Besiktas y el CSKA Moscú, que terminó con una contundente victoria turca por 80-57. Mediado el último cuarto, el jugador canadiense-nigeriano se enzarzó con el base ruso Ivan Ukhov después de un enfrentamiento entre ambos. Omoruyi fue quien inició la pelea al propinar una bofetada a Ukhov, que respondió inmediatamente con otro golpe en la cara. Los compañeros y los árbitros tuvieron que intervenir para separarles y ambos jugadores acabaron expulsados. El incidente también provocó la expulsión del capitán del CSKA, Semyon Antonov, que salió en defensa de su compañero. Omoruyi, de 1,98 m y 29 años, afronta así su primera temporada en el Besiktas después de jugar la 2025-26 en el Baskonia, donde promedió 8,8 puntos, 2,5 rebotes y 1,6 asistencias en la Liga Endesa.

articles.title: Former NFL Star Edgerrin James Says Son Jizzle Has a Substance Abuse Issue; Asks for Love, Support
articles.summary: CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — Former NFL running back Edgerrin James posted a message on Instagram expressing concern and urging support for his college basketball-playing son Jizzle James, who he said is dealing with a substance abuse issue.
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — Former NFL running back Edgerrin James posted a message on Instagram expressing concern and urging support for his college basketball-playing son Jizzle James, who he said is dealing with a substance abuse issue.

James wrote on social media that Jizzle "is not in the right state of mind right now. If you see him, show him love, but do not give him money, valuables, or anything material. You're not helping him by feeding the problem. He wants/needs for nothing."

SEC Leaders to Discuss Kicking LSU Out (AP)

"Give him a hug. Give him encouragement. Give him love. That's it. Be patient with him," James said. "We're fighting for him, not against him."

Jizzle James spent the last three seasons with Cincinnati but transferred earlier this offseason to Charlotte after head coach Wes Miller left the Bearcats and was hired by the 49ers.

A member of the Charlotte sports information staff confirmed James is no longer with the program.

Cincinnati dismissed James from the program last summer before he was brought back on the roster midway through the season. He played in 23 games last season averaging 10.9 points and 2.1 assists per game for the Bearcats.

articles.title: Phil Jackson to Be Honored by Lakers with Statue, Reveal Date Announced for 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: One of the greatest coaches in NBA history will soon be honored with a statue outside of the stadium where he spent some of his best days.
articles.body:
One of the greatest coaches in NBA history will soon be honored with a statue outside of the stadium where he spent some of his best days.

Phil Jackson is set to be honored with a statue outside of Crypto.com Arena this season, and the statue will be unveiled on April 9 ahead of the Los Angeles Lakers' matchup against the Minnesota Timberwolves, the team announced on Tuesday.

Jackson had a 14-year playing career in the NBA before stepping into the coaching world in the late 1970s. He took over as the Chicago Bulls' head coach in 1989 and went on to win six titles with Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen, establishing one of the greatest dynasties in sports history.

Jackson's coaching career appeared to be over after his "Last Dance" season with the Bulls in 1998, but he returned to the NBA a year later as the head coach of the Lakers.

Leading the iconic duo of Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O'Neal, Jackson won three consecutive championships in 2000, 2001 and 2002. He left the Lakers after the 2003-04 season, which ended with a Finals loss to the Detroit Pistons.

Just one season later, Jackson returned to Los Angeles as the head coach of the Lakers. His second tenure wasn't quite as dominant as his first, but he still led the team to titles in 2009 and 2010, with Bryant leading the way. He retired from coaching following the 2010-11 season.

"Phil Jackson defines championship basketball for a reason," Lakers governor Jeanie Buss said in a statement . "His masterful approach to coaching brought out the best in some of the greatest athletes to ever play the game. After he accepted my dad's invitation to join the Lakers, Phil's unmatched creativity and commitment to excellence restored our championship legacy, bringing five titles and setting a standard of excellence for generations to come. It is a great joy to be able to mark that achievement with the statue he so richly deserves."

Jackson will become the ninth member of the Lakers with a statue outside of the arena, joining Bryant, O'Neal, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Elgin Baylor, Chick Hearn, Magic Johnson, Pat Riley and Jerry West.

articles.title: Familiar face leads Hungary on historic run to FIBA World Cup quarterfinal against USA Basketball
articles.summary: Forward Dorka Juhasz, of the WNBA's Minnesota Lynx, helped Hungary reach the FIBA World Cup quarterfinals, where they'll face Team USA.
articles.body:
BERLIN — Hungary's national team made history inside Berlin Arena on Tuesday evening, reaching the quarterfinals of the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup for the first time in 40 years with a 84-63 victory over Japan. Hungary's punched ticket will lead to the challenge of facing four-time defending champion United States at 5:30 a.m. Thursday with the hope of medaling for the first time in team history.

Hungary led for 39:39 by making 28 of 56 shots, including 11 of 25 from beyond the arc. Guard Reka Lelik led Hungary with 23 points and tied Virag Takacs-Kiss in rebounds with eight. Hungary held Japan to 32% shooting, including 7 for 33 from 3-point range. Hungary also improved upon its turnover ratio, committing 17 turnovers, a team low in the tournament.

"It's been 40 years since we went to the quarterfinals. I still can't believe it," Lelik said. "I'm in huge shock, but this was really a big team effort."

Now, as Hungary sets its sights on the U.S., the victory over Japan created momentum to fight for a spot on the podium.

"I think it is going to be a great game for us," Hungary forward Dorka Juhasz said. "Not many times has Hungary faced the USA in any shape or form, so I think it is going to be fun. We are going to bring our heart, our fight, and give all we have in that game."

Juhasz, a 6-foot-4 forward, should be familiar to U.S. fans through her play for the Minnesota Lynx of the WNBA. In World Cup play, Juhasz has averaged 15.3 points per game and ranked third in the tournament with 11 rebounds.

See Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston photos in FIBA Women's World Cup

Before the matchup against Japan, Juhasz had recorded a double-double in each of her three women's World Cup appearances. She scored 10 points with seven rebounds, falling just shy of becoming the first World Cup player to post four consecutive double-doubles since records were first kept in 1994.

Juhasz will see several familiar faces when she steps out onto the hardwood on Thursday, but none more prominent than former UConn teammate Paige Bueckers . They shared time as teammates during Bueckers' sophomore season, 2021-22 season, and the 2022-23 season. Bueckers sat out of the 2022-23 season due to a knee injury; however, her connection with Juhasz is more than apparent.

"I always love to play against her; we are always joking around, but this is a different setting," Juhasz said. "We did that in the WNBA, and now we are in Europe. I'm just excited to see us representing our country and just compete against each other and have some fun."

Although Juhasz's remarks about her former teammate made it clear how competitive they both are, she also made their unbreakable bond known and the love that runs much deeper than wins and losses.

"That is my sister," Juhasz said. "I think that bond we made in UConn is never going away. Hopefully one day we are going to be teammates again as well. And every time we play against each other, we catch up, and that's family, so I think that's something that will always be there no matter where we are, and I am just excited to see her."

Hungary's best finish in tournament history was fifth place in 1957. Reaching the 16-team World Cup field was an achievement for Hungary, which lost two of its first three games in a qualifying tournament before defeating Argentina and Turkiye at Istanbul. The coaches and players watched their quarterfinal opponent escape in the 55-52 U.S. victory over Italy.

Lelik remarked on Italy's ability to control the pace and dominate on defense. As a team, they have taken a few lessons from the Italians.

"What Italy did on defense, it was amazing," Lelik said. "I think we need to continue what they did … But with defense, we need to focus for 40 minutes; we cannot lose focus for a second. And then, offensively, we need to be brave against them."

Hungary coach Peter Volgyi smiled as he had another suggestion:

"We can learn from every game, basically," Volgyi said through an interpreter, "but coach thinks that we need one very, you know, extra performance from one of our players to be able to match them."

articles.title: Elisa Aguilar: "Estoy convencida de que vamos a hacer algo grande"
articles.standfirst: Con la selección ya entre las ocho mejores del Mundial Femenino, la presidenta de la FEB visualiza la cuarta medalla en el torneo
articles.summary: Con la selección ya entre las ocho mejores del Mundial Femenino, la presidenta de la FEB visualiza la cuarta medalla en el torneo
articles.body: Con España ya metida entre las ocho mejores del Mundial Femenino, Elisa Aguilar (Madrid, 1976), presidenta de la FEB, pasa revista a la selección antes de los cruces y no puede estar más ilusionada con lo que ve y, sobre todo, con lo que siente con un equipo especial. Pese a los grandes obstáculos -Australia o Italia y después seguramente Estados Unidos-, se ve en el podio. Pregunta. Primer objetivo cumplido estando directamente en cuartos. Respuesta. Sí. Cuando empiezas este tipo de campeonatos, tienes objetivos por cubrir y el primero, obviamente, era estar en cuartos mejor que en octavos. Se ha dado y ahora, viendo lo que se está dando, te das cuenta de que tampoco era fácil. P. ¿Hubo algún momento de nerviosismo tras perder ante Mali? ¿Pensaron que se habían metido en un lío? R. Iniciamos el campeonato con partido completo a todos los niveles que fue un subidón. Luego jugamos contra Mali, a la que acabamos de ganar en Zaragoza relativamente fácil, pero jugamos con pocas horas de descanso. No tuvimos ni 24 y aquí la exigencia de todos los partidos es máxima. Ellas jugaron muy bien, muy físico y nosotros no nos encontramos cómodos. ¿Nos esperábamos la derrota? Pues no. ¿Creo que nos ha venido bien? Pues yo creo que sí. El partido contra Japón fue incomodísimo y complicado por la presión pero lo sacamos bien. Somos un equipo en formación, con mucho futuro, con muy buen presente, pero si no estamos al cien por cien, cualquier selección puede ganarte. Entonces, no te voy a negar que siempre hay un poco de incertidumbre, un par de horas en algún momento, pero hay confianza plena en que tenemos un equipo para ganar y así lo hicimos contra Japón. P. ¿Han hablado con FIBA por el poco descanso que tuvieron? R. Se comentó con ellos, pero así es el calendario de un torneo corto. En este caso no salimos favorecidos y lo deberán analizar. De cara al futuro, no puede ser que haya selecciones que no tengan un mínimo de descanso por respeto a la salud de las jugadoras. Seguro que estas situaciones se irán ajustando y no se repetirán. P. Mirando el cuadro, vaya cruces se han quedado para haber sido líderes... Australia o Italia y luego Estados Unidos. R. Si quieres llegar lejos, te van a tocar equipos potentes y con mucho talento. Vamos a ver si es Italia o Australia, y, si todo va bien, lo lógico es que fuera Estados Unidos. Nosotras vamos con todo el respeto del mundo contra todas, pero miedo ninguno. Eso lo dicen nuestras jugadoras. P. Viendo la primera fase, parece que Estados Unidos igual es más asequible que otros años y que el coco es Francia R. Es que en los Juegos de París ya estuvo muy cerquita. Estados Unidos es un equipazo siempre y ahora mismo las francesas están también a su nivel, pero, yo confío en mi equipo y creo que nuestro talento es el grupo. Ahí está nuestra fortaleza. Eso es lo mejor que tenemos. P. ¿En el vestuario se habla de medallas? R. En un torneo así, soñar es gratis. Seguramente las jugadoras tengan en la cabeza colgarse una medalla. Eso dice mucho de su mentalidad ganadora, pero para que pase eso saben que vamos a tener que sufrir y que jugar contra equipazos. No es malo hablar de medallas, no es presión, sino ilusión y motivación. P. ¿Y de cualquier color? R. Si soñar es gratis, vamos a soñar a lo grande. Estados Unidos es mi favorita, Australia es un equipazo e Italia nos ha ganado los últimas emparejamientos, pero sabemos de nuestras responsabilidades, sabemos el ADN que tenemos, que es no bajar nunca los brazos, humildad, trabajo y equipo tanto dentro como fuera. P. Fue internacional 222 veces y ha seguido siempre a la selección. ¿Había visto una España tan especial? R. Hemos tenido equipos muy especiales que han hecho cosas muy grandes a lo largo de nuestra historia, pero ahora estamos en un momento muy dulce del baloncesto femenino: de selección, de jugadoras jóvenes que están yendo a la NBA... El envoltorio también es muy atractivo y muy visual. La Liga Femenina Endesa es la mejor Liga de Europa. Yo creo que se están dando unos condicionantes que hacen que todo sea especial. Y es que las jugadoras son muy especiales como equipo. Las jóvenes son amigas y se alegran de que a una le vaya bien. Las veteranas saben perfectamente su papel y están encantadas de estar con esta generación que apunta muy bien. Y también, siempre lo digo, tener a Miguel [Méndez] de maestro en el banquillo hace que todo sea muy natural y muy normal. Se pondera el equipo y el grupo, que es fundamental lo que hace que España pueda estar, por lo menos, compitiendo con las grandes selecciones. P. Usted, por ejemplo, con 20 años estaba en el Canoe. Iyana y Awa, con 20 años, son las mejores anotadoras de la selección en un Mundial con 17,3 y 12,3 puntos, respectivamente, e Iyana es la cuarta mejor del torneo. Son otra cosa. R. Son jugadoras a las que llevábamos viendo desde muy jóvenes en selecciones de formación y en campeonatos de España. Son de estas jugadoras que, aparte de talento, tienen algo más. Encima, son de la misma generación. Pero ellas solas no podrían hacer todo lo que han hecho y espero que en un futuro harán. El ecosistema de sus compañeras, sus clubes, sus familias, la FEB... está muy alineado con ellas. Los números que me dices están al alcance de muy pocas jugadoras a su edad y estoy convencida de que van a seguir así, sobre todo cuando las conoces. Tiene mucha humildad y mucha capacidad de trabajo. Tienen los pies en el suelo, que no es fácil a la edad que tienen y con lo que están viviendo. Eso es magnífico. Tenemos mucha suerte de tenerlas en la selección. Es una bendición. P. ¿Siente envidia? ¿Le gustaría estar ahí? R. No siento envidia porque tengo el privilegio de ser la presidenta. El pasado de los años lo llevo con total naturalidad. En mi momento lo disfruté mucho. Fui una afortunada porque también gané muchos premios para la selección y viví experiencias irrepetibles y geniales. Ahora estoy viviendo otras experiencias como presidenta y es un privilegio poder estar con ellas, ver cómo interactúan, cómo son un equipo con los entrenadores, con todo el staff y ver lo que transmiten. La verdad es que nada de envidia. P. ¿Hay alguna jugadora con la que se sienta identificada? Por el juego, por el carácter... R. No lo había pensado. Somos muy distintas. A lo mejor por base, por ese tipo de juego, puede que Maite [Cazorla]. Afortunadamente, todas ellas son mucho mejores lo que era yo. Tienen mucho más talento y eso me hace infinitamente feliz. P. Espero que volvamos a hablar el próximo lunes en una celebración. R. Esto es un sueño y me ilusiono. Me motiva toda la gente que tenemos aquí. Luego, claro, pasará lo que tenga que pasar, pero el gusto de poder vivir un momento de cuartos de final no lo tiene todo el mundo. Por supuesto que yo confío en mi equipo. Confío en ellas y en el staff técnico y estoy convencida de que vamos a hacer algo grande.

articles.title: Craig Carton, Michael Rapaport dish on their shared dislike for LeBron James: 'Dead to me'
articles.summary: Craig Carton and Michael Rapaport revealed their reasons for disliking LeBron James during the premiere of OutKick's "The Craig Carton Show."
articles.body: Craig Carton and Michael Rapaport have more in common than being die-hard New York Knicks fans: They also share a strong dislike for LeBron James. Rapaport joined Carton for the premiere of OutKick’s "The Craig Carton Show" releasing on Tuesday, where he called the Philadelphia 76ers star a player he loves to hate. Carton admitted that while he respects James’ game, his No. 1 reason for his dislike stems from an off-the-court incident in 2017. "I'll tell you the number one reason I'm not a LeBron guy. Number one. There's—it's and it's a clear-cut number one for me, and I think I'm the only guy that views it this way, and it p----es me off, all right. Years ago, when he was in Cleveland, and our country is going through racial issues," Carton said on the premiere of his new show. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "In my opinion, he invented a story that the people spray-painted racial epithets on the gate leading up his driveway." The Associated Press reported at the time, citing police, that unidentified vandals spray-painted the N-Word on the front gate of James' $20 million home in Brentwood. Police said the incident was reported at around 6:45 a.m. local time and nearly three hours later property management covered it up. No arrests were ever made. Carton said that he believed James used the event as a vehicle to include himself in the larger conversation at the time. "And to me, I'm like, look, there's real racial issues in our country. We acknowledge them. For a guy who's such a prominent African-American to try to get in on the conversation by inventing something that never took place. Dead to me," Carton said. "No one talks about it. It's been forgotten because it never happened. No one has the balls to ask—ask him about it, and I'm like, how do we forget the fact that he intruded himself into this serious conversation about race?" The actor said he had been cool with James and that they had first met during his rookie year with the Cleveland Cavaliers. A few years later, Rapaport was with his kids, who were 5 and 7 at the time, and James spurned the kids' request for a picture. "I don't know what he got up bug up his a-- about Michael Rapaport. I had never said anything bad about him. Never said anything," Rapaport said. "I brought my little kids. They were like five and seven, right? And he like Heismaned." After that point, Rapaport was turned off by James. Prior to the incident with his kids, Rapaport said he had never said anything bad about the then-Cavaliers star. And I think it was a rumor that a friend of mine might have a girl with a friend, and I was like, that has nothing to do with—these are little kids. And that was when I was like, ‘You’re done,’" Rapaport said. With James joining the 76ers this offseason, Carton and Rapaport, both passionate Knicks fans, will get to see a lot more of the 41-year-old this season. The 76ers' first game of the season is against the defending champions at Madison Square Garden. Carton’s show launched Sept. 8 and will feature A-list guests with takes on sports and world events.

articles.title: “Simply Not The Best Point Guard” – WNBA Broadcaster Raises Questions Over Kara Lawson’s FIBA World Cup Tactics
articles.summary: Team USA may have swept the group stage, but fans and experts are still not convinced by their starting lineup and rotations at the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketb...
articles.body:
Team USA may have swept the group stage, but fans and experts are still not convinced by their starting lineup and rotations at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup . Joining the conversation is Sports Illustrated's Robin Lundberg, who isn't convinced by Kara Lawson's tactics.

In a recent video on his YouTube channel , Lundberg bluntly expressed his concerns about Chelsea Gray starting for the American team. While he acknowledged Gray's experience and clutch factor, keeping both Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers on the bench doesn't sit well with him.

The American broadcaster said, "The biggest issue that I think most people are having with Team USA is the lineup distribution and the rotations. And Chelsea Gray is just simply not the best point guard on the team."

Lundberg further made his case by presenting statistics for all three point guards. He acknowledged that the sample size was only three games, but the numbers still reflected what Clark and Bueckers bring to the table.

The American broadcaster highlighted that both Clark and Bueckers lead the team in point differential when they are on the court. He also noted that both point guards rank at the top of the list in assists.

Lundberg's assessment certainly raises questions about Kara Lawson's rotation decisions. Team USA will next face Hungary in the FIBA World Cup quarterfinals. If everything goes well, the Americans might face Spain or the winner of Italy vs. Australia in the semifinals.

Kara Lawson Needs Caitlin Clark And Paige Bueckers In The Lineup

While Clark seems to be struggling at the FIBA World Cup , experts believe it is largely because of the limited playing time she has received throughout the group stage. According to Lundberg, the Iowa native has been effective despite her short time on the court, especially when playing alongside Paige Bueckers.

Highlighting additional statistics, Lundberg pointed out that "the most effective lineups" have included both Clark and Bueckers. The best lineup featured both point guards alongside Angel Reese , Aliyah Boston , and Rhyne Howard , posting a +76.4 rating.

Lundberg believes that Kara Lawson needs to settle on the right lineup if Team USA plans to win every knockout game and reach the final. He also thinks France will reach the gold-medal game, and that is when Team USA will need its best lineup, which might not include Jackie Young , Chelsea Gray, and Kahleah Cooper.

articles.title: Giannis Buys $13.5M Miami Mansion After Heat Trade, Photos Showcase Pool, Outdoor Kitchen, More
articles.summary: After being traded to the Miami Heat earlier this summer, Giannis Antetokounmpo has found a home in his new city.
articles.body:
After being traded to the Miami Heat earlier this summer, Giannis Antetokounmpo has found a home in his new city.

The former Milwaukee Bucks star purchased a $13.5 million mansion in Miami this week.

According to Catherine Odom of the Miami Herald , the house is in the Pinewood suburb of South Miami-Dade. It has eight bedrooms and sits on a one-acre lot. The mansion features a swimming pool, an outdoor kitchen and more.

Odom noted that the house is right around the corner from the house Tyler Herro — who was traded to Milwaukee in the package for Antetokounmpo — is currently selling for $12 million.

Antetokounmpo, a two-time MVP who brought a championship to Milwaukee, will team up with star center Bam Adebayo and Andrew Wiggins and look to deliver a title to the Heat. Miami also signed sharpshooting veteran Klay Thompson this offseason.

Antetokounmpo turns any roster into a championship contender, so it's safe to say there are lofty expectations for the Heat heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

articles.title: 5 NBA Teams That Got Better This Offseason, and 5 That Got Worse
articles.summary: The late stages of the NBA offseason continue to bring us some excitement and have helped decipher which teams truly got better or worse.
articles.body:
The late stages of the NBA offseason continue to bring us some excitement and have helped decipher which teams truly got better or worse.

In the last few weeks we've seen Peyton Watson become a Cleveland Cavalier, DeMar DeRozan sign with the Denver Nuggets, Jonathan Kuminga team up with Anthony Edwards with the Minnesota Timberwolves and Klay Thompson agree to leave the Dallas Mavericks for the sunny beaches of Miami, Florida. Oh, and Ben Simmons is back in the NBA.

We're going to ignore some of the obvious teams for this exercise, as the Indiana Pacers and Philadelphia 76ers should be way better than 2025-26 while the Giannis Antetokounmpo-less Milwaukee Bucks will sink to the bottom of the NBA.

Instead, let's zero in on 10 of the NBA's most interesting teams and determine if they actually got better or worse this offseason.

Notable Additions: PF John Collins, SG Isaiah Joe, F Taurean Prince, SG Gary Harris, PG Ebuka Okorie (R)

Notable Subtractions: PF Tobias Harris, F/C Isaiah Stewart, G/F Caris LeVert

The Detroit Pistons' 60 wins earned them the No. 1 seed in the East last season. This year, there's a real chance they fall all the way to the play-in tournament.

This is both a credit to the conference as a whole and a knock on the Pistons, who have done nothing to actually improve this offseason as we await for the Jalen Duren free agency saga to come to a conclusion. Duren remains unsigned and Stewart was salary dumped on the Memphis Grizzlies, leaving (for the moment) a huge hole at the center position.

Collins is a borderline starter/sixth man at this stage of his career who had a swing rating of minus-4.6 (30th percentile via Cleaning the Glass ) for the Los Angeles Clippers last year. Swapping him in for Tobias Harris is about as neutral a move as it gets. Given that he's been the Pistons' big addition thus far is concerning, especially for a team that seemed destined to become a powerhouse in the East.

Would we be shocked if the New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Indiana Pacers, Cleveland Cavaliers, Toronto Raptors, Miami Heat, Boston Celtics and Atlanta Hawks all finished above the Pistons? That's eight teams, and we haven't even mentioned up-and-coming franchises like the Orlando Magic, Charlotte Hornets or Washington Wizards yet.

Headlined by the NBA champs and a number of other contenders who made significant moves this offseason, the East is actually pretty legit. That's bad news for the Pistons, who will be lucky to hit 50 wins this time around.

Notable Additions: F Caleb Wilson (R), SG Norman Powell, C Nic Claxton, F Dailyn Swain (R)

Notable Subtractions: G Anfernee Simons, G Collin Sexton

The Chicago Bulls aren't going to make the East playoffs this season, but a spot in the play-in tournament isn't out of the question.

Defense should be improved this year by swapping Claxton in place of Nikola Vučević. Chicago's defensive rating of 117.4 ranked 22nd overall, with Vučević's defensive swing rating of plus-4.5 ranking in the 18th percentile . Claxton is younger, more mobile and offers far greater rim protection overall.

A backcourt of Josh Giddey and Powell is very solid and Wilson looked like a future All-Star during summer league. Matas Buzelis, 21, is coming off a breakout sophomore season where he averaged 16.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 blocks in 29.2 minutes per game.

New head coach Tiago Splitter proved his worth last season as an interim with the Portland Trail Blazers, guiding them to a winning record without an injured Damian Lillard and helping Deni Avdija make his first All-Star game.

This is a franchise that's finally headed in the right direction and could finish with 40-plus wins, even in a tough East.

Notable Additions: F DeMar DeRozan, F/C Marvin Bagley III

Notable Subtractions: SF Peyton Watson, C Jonas Valančiūnas, SG Tim Hardaway Jr.

The sky isn't falling for the Denver Nuggets just yet. Nikola Jokić is still the best player in the NBA and Jamal Murray is coming off the best season of his career. For a team that's struggled to build depth and defense around their stars for years, however, this summer was a major step back.

Not being able to afford to keep Peyton Watson is a huge blow to the team, as the 23-year-old developed into one of the better young two-way wings in the NBA during his four seasons with the Nuggets. Valančiūnas finally gave this team some stability at center behind Jokić and Hardaway left in free agency after finishing third in Sixth Man of the Year voting. Bruce Brown Jr. remains a free agent.

While the starting five is still one of the NBA's best, this bench looks rough.

DeRozan is 37 and could be entering the final year of his career. He's not a good defender or three-point shooter, which is what Denver needs in its rotation. Bagley will try to absorb the backup center minutes, but he's a journeyman who's now on his sixth team in six years.

Denver could still get to 50 wins if their stars stay healthy, but this is putting a lot on Jokić heading into unrestricted free agency next summer. The Nuggets are playing with fire.

Notable Additions: F Lu Dort, G Aaron Wiggins, PG Ryan Nembhard, G Devin Carter, G Kingston Flemings, C Zuby Ejiofor

Notable Subtractions: G/F Zaccharie Risacher

The Atlanta Hawks may have the NBA's best defense this season.

A 108.6 rating after the All-Star break following the trade of Trae Young was second only to the Oklahoma City Thunder, the team Atlanta has now plucked both Dort and Wiggins away from. Dort finished fourth in Defensive Player of the Year voting in 2024-25 and is still only 27 years old. He's a tough, physical defensive who can guard multiple positions that the Hawks can plug into a lineup alongside guys like Dyson Daniels, Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Onyeka Okongwu.

The guard position has been revamped post-Young, as Flemings, the No. 8 overall pick this summer, gets to learn behind CJ McCollum for at least a year. Carter and Nembhard bring some added defense and playmaking to the backcourt as well.

This Hawks team is deep, has a bonafide All-Star in Jalen Johnson and blends some veteran talent with enough young talent to inspire a bright future.

This is a dark horse to come away with the No. 1 seed in the East, as the team's defense will now be elite all season long.

Notable Additions: F Yaxel Lendeborg, F Georges Niang

The Golden State Warriors are going to miss the West play-in tournament next year and it's not going to feel right.

After a decade-plus of titles, playoff runs and some unbelievably-beautiful basketball, the Warriors are headed for an inevitable collapse. Jimmy Butler will likely miss months with a torn ACL, and the team went just 14-30 in his absence last year with a net rating of minus-4.8 in all non-Butler minutes.

The players brought in to hold down the fort, Lendeborg and Niang, are either playing in their first NBA games or coming off a season-long foot injury. Neither logged a minute of NBA basketball last season.

An average player age of 29.2 is the oldest in the NBA , with Stephen Curry set to turn 39 before the season ends.

This is a franchise that needed to make some bold moves this offseason to save what was left of the dynasty. Curry will want to end his career as a Warrior, although NBA fans should want to see him join a new team that actually has a chance to win a championship.

Notable Additions: PF Cameron Boozer (R), F Jerami Grant, F/C Isaiah Stewart, F Karim López (R)

Notable Subtractions: PG Ja Morant, F/C Santi Aldama

Credit to the Memphis Grizzlies for realizing that their previous core had hit its peak and that pivoting to a rebuild was the right move. If Zach Edey can shake off his previous injury woes, this team will be back to revelancy soon.

The Grizzlies went 7-4 in Edey's 11 games last season, as the 7'3" center put up 13.6 points, 11.1 rebounds, 1.9 blocks and shot 63.3 percent overall in just 25.8 minutes. With the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder seemingly in a size race, the Grizzlies' have the NBA's biggest player on their roster.

An Edey-Boozer frontcourt could be dangerous for the next decade. Boozer should be the Rookie of the Year favorite, as the 19-year-old is already entering the league with a polished offensive game. With an elite rim protector next to him, Boozer doesn't face the same defensive pressure as a lot of the other top picks.

Grant wasn't the return the Grizzlies were hoping for when shopping Morant, although the veteran wing is still playing at a high level. In his 38 starts for the Portland Trail Blazers, Grant averaged 19.7 points and shot 40.2 percent from three. Between Boozer, Grant, Edey, Cedric Coward and Ty Jerome, this offense should be way better than the unit that finished just 23rd overall last season.

Aldama and Stewart give this frontcourt even more muscle and depth in case Edey has to miss more time. The Grizzlies already have a strong foundation and will soar past 30 wins this season.

Notable Additions: C Walker Kessler, G Collin Sexton, G/F Quentin Grimes, F/C Sandro Mamukelashvili, C Kevon Looney, G/F Matisse Thybulle, SG Cameron Carr (R)

Notable Subtractions: F LeBron James, C Deandre Ayton, F Rui Hachimura, G Marcus Smart, F Luke Kennard

Over half of the Los Angeles Lakers' roster will be brand new in 2026-27. That's a startling change that now leaves Austin Reaves as the franchise's longest-tenured player at just five seasons.

Did the Lakers put better-fitting pieces around Luka Dončić? Yes.

Is this team more talented overall and should expect more than 53 wins? No.

Watching an All-Star forward who averaged over 20 points, six rebounds and seven assists walk out the door in free agency would be difficult for any team, and that's ignoring all of the coaching, knowledge and experience that LeBron James brought to this franchise. His salary coming off the books led to a lot of these signings, although Los Angeles had to deal out some hefty contracts that may be tough to trade down the road if needed.

Kessler is a huge rim-protecting center who can rebound and may be developing an outside shot, although he's had a negative offensive swing rating in his last two healthy seasons and played just five games in 2025-26 due to shoulder surgery. Giving up multiple first-round picks and pick swaps to acquire him in a sign-and-trade severely limits the Lakers' ability to make any real improvements in the near future.

Los Angeles assembled a solid rotation around Dončić, who's going to put up monster numbers this season with James gone. For a Lakers franchise historically built on star power, however, this roster comes up short.

Notable Additions: PG Ja Morant, PG Damian Lillard (return from injury)

Notable Subtractions: F Jerami Grant, G/F Matisse Thybulle

Rolling the dice on Morant was a risk worth taking, as the 27-year-old only has two years remaining on his contract. If he can return to All-Star form, great. If not, the Portland Trail Blazers will have an expiring $44.9 million contract to play with next season.

Despite making the playoffs, the Blazers' offense ranked just 21st overall last year, an even worse mark than the 26-win New Orleans Pelicans. Now with Morant and the return of Lillard for the first time in three years, there'll be plenty of juice coming out of the backcourt.

Scoot Henderson is playing for a new contract and should still see plenty of minutes when Lillard gets a night off or Morant inevitably misses some time due to injury. Jrue Holiday quietly had another strong season even at age 35, averaging 16.3 points, 4.6 rebounds, 6.1 assists and shooting 37.8 percent from three in less than 30 minutes a game.

Donovan Clingan is one of the few players who can rival the size of Victor Wembanyama, as the 7'2", 280-pound center led the NBA in offensive rebounds last year (4.5 per game). In his first season as a full-time starter, the 22-year-old averaged 12.1 points, 11.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.7 blocks while showing some three-point ability (34.1 percent on 3.2 attempts per game).

Led by All-Star forward Deni Avdija and one of the league's most versatile defenders in Toumani Camara, there's a lot to like about this Blazers team on the rise.

Notable Additions: PG LaMelo Ball, F Jonathan Kuminga, F Cody Williams

Notable Subtractions: PF Julius Randle, F/C Naz Reid, PG Mike Conley Jr., F Kyle Anderson

One can understand why the Minnesota Timberwolves swung for the fences for a talent like Ball. Back-to-back sub-50 win seasons and a second-place exit in the playoffs may have led to a restless Anthony Edwards, especially without a dependable running mate to share the offensive load.

Essentially losing Randle, Reid, four first-round picks and swaps and three second-round picks in order to acquire Ball is way too risky of a move to make, however, especially for a franchise already thin on trade assets.

Ball has played more than 51 games just twice in his six-year career. If he gets hurt again, Ayo Dosunmu is the only other reliable guard now that Donte DiVincenzo is out with a torn ACL and Conley left for the Boston Celtics in free agency.

Kuminga is now on his third team in seven months. A two-year, $12.4 million contract was a no-brainer for Minnesota to offer, although it's fair to question if the 23-year-old will be willing to play a 3-and-D role that the Wolves need or look to pump up his own individual numbers in search of the pay day he's long sought after.

Losing Randle and Reid hurt this team's size and overall scoring. Conley was a beloved veteran in the locker room and young forwards like Kuminga and Williams haven't proven they can help a team actually win games.

If Ball deals with more injury issues, things could go south in The North Star State, fast.

Notable Additions: SG Darryn Peterson, G/F Josh Okogie, G/F Josh Green, C Jaxson Hayes

Notable Subtractions: C Walker Kessler, F Cody Williams

The Utah Jazz may double their win total this season, a feat that maybe only the Indiana Pacers could also accomplish.

A full season of Jaren Jackson Jr. will do wonders to improve a defense that ranked 29th overall in the NBA last year. The 26-year-old has led the league in blocks twice, been named to three All-Defensive teams and was the 2022-23 Defensive Player of the Year. Pairing him with Jusuf Nurkić in the frontcourt helps make up for Jackson's lack of rebounding, and Nurkić was really good as a starter last year (11.3 points, 10.8 rebounds, 5.1 assists, 37.7 percent shooting from three).

Peterson, Keyonte George and Ace Bailey is an exciting young offensive trio to build around. They'll need to establish some sort of pecking order, although Peterson, this June's No. 2 overall pick, will likely come out on top.

Lauri Markkanen is still around and coming off an awesome year (26.7 points) and there's still a fair amount of young talent on this roster that can all make a leap.

Simply trying to win games will go a long way for the Jazz this season. The fog is clearing from a four-year rebuild, one that now has Utah set up for sustained success.

articles.title: NBA trade news: Memphis Grizzlies add $20.6 million former UConn star from New Orleans Pelicans to pair with Cameron Boozer
articles.summary: NBA News: Jordan Hawkins is heading to Memphis to join Cameron Boozer. The 24-year-old guard was dealt from New Orleans to the Grizzlies on Tuesday in a trade f.
articles.body: Jordan Hawkins is heading to Memphis to join Cameron Boozer. The 24-year-old guard was dealt from New Orleans to the Grizzlies on Tuesday in a trade first reported by ESPN's Shams Charania, with forward Micah Peavy, a future second-round pick and a second-round pick swap also headed to Memphis. In return, the Pelicans land AJ Johnson and veteran forward Taj Gibson.The deal has roots in late July, when whispers first emerged that New Orleans was exploring trade frameworks to move Hawkins and create financial breathing room. Memphis, which has spent the past year hoarding draft capital and young talent, turned out to be the perfect landing spot.CategoryDetailsPlayer traded to GrizzliesJordan Hawkins, Micah PeavyDraft compensation to GrizzliesOne future second-round pick, one second-round pick swapPlayers traded to PelicansAJ Johnson, Taj GibsonPrevious teamNew Orleans PelicansNew teamMemphis GrizzliesContract status (Hawkins)One year remaining, 2026-27 seasonSalary cap hit (Hawkins)$7,021,895Memphis Grizzlies land Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy and two draft assets from the PelicansNew Orleans had been shopping $20.6 million former UConn star Jordan Hawkins for weeks, according to Marc Stein and Jake Fischer of The Stein Line, who reported on July 22 that the Pelicans were working through trade frameworks to move him. Michael Scotto of HoopsHype added on July 31 that Johnson had entered those discussions as well. The pieces finally came together Tuesday.For New Orleans, the trade clears space to get Bennedict Mathurin's new contract on the books, a priority that made moving Hawkins almost inevitable. He still had one year and roughly $7 million left on his rookie deal, a manageable number that made him easy to move without much resistance.Memphis, meanwhile, keeps building its war chest. The Grizzlies now hold ten tradable second-round picks and twelve first-round picks across the next seven drafts, nine of which they can deal. Giving up AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson was a small price for a team this deep in assets.What adding Jordan Hawkins means for the Memphis GrizzliesHawkins lands in Memphis carrying more upside than his recent numbers suggest. The Pelicans picked him 14th overall in the 2023 draft, just three months after he helped UConn win a national championship. His rookie season showed flashes of that promise, averaging 7.8 points and shooting 36.6 percent from three across 67 games. His signature moment came against Dallas in January 2024, when he dropped a career-high 34 points in a Pelicans win.His role shrank after that. Last season he played just 51 games, started only once, and averaged 5.1 points in limited minutes. Even so, a career 37.4 percent shooter from the field has value, and Memphis is betting it can unlock the version of Hawkins that torched the NCAA Tournament at 50 percent from deep. If that shooter shows up, the Grizzlies just found themselves a bargain.How the trade could impact the New Orleans PelicansFor New Orleans, this trade is less about what they got and more about what it lets them do next. Offloading Hawkins' salary gives the front office room to lock in Bennedict Mathurin, a move that has been the underlying goal of these talks since July.AJ Johnson gives the Pelicans a young guard already familiar to their front office from earlier trade conversations, while Taj Gibson brings a steady, experienced presence to a locker room that could use one. articles.summary: Phil Jackson's statue will join nine others at Star Plaza, honoring the coach who delivered five titles with Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O'Neal.
articles.body: Phil Jackson, who won five of his record 11 NBA coaching titles with the Los Angeles Lakers, will be honored with a statue, the team confirmed Tuesday. "Phil Jackson defines championship basketball for a reason," Lakers acting governor Jeanie Buss said in a statement. When the statue honoring Jackson is unveiled before an April game during the 2026-27 season, he will become the ninth member of the Lakers immortalized in bronze at Star Plaza outside the Lakers’ downtown Los Angeles home. "His masterful approach to coaching brought out the best in some of the greatest athletes to ever play the game. After he accepted my dad's invitation to join the Lakers, Phil's unmatched creativity and commitment to excellence restored our championship legacy, bringing five titles and setting a standard of excellence for generations to come." The statement called Jackson deserving of the honor for his storied career. "It is a great joy to be able to mark that achievement with the statue he so richly deserves." Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Famers Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O’Neal powered the three-peat title run. Bryant remained the centerpiece for the final two championships, with Pau Gasol joining him as the other cornerstone. Jackson was enshrined in the Basketball Hall of Fame as part of the 2007 class. articles.title: NBA trade news: Philadelphia 76ers add 6-foot-5 New York Knicks champion to pair with LeBron James
articles.summary: NBA News: Dillon Jones is bringing his rings to Philadelphia. The 76ers signed the 24-year-old forward to an Exhibit 10 contract on Tuesday, ESPN's Dave McMenam.
articles.body: Dillon Jones is bringing his rings to Philadelphia. The 76ers signed the 24-year-old forward to an Exhibit 10 contract on Tuesday, ESPN's Dave McMenamin first reported, giving Jones a shot to win a training camp roster spot. Jones spent last season with the Knicks after winning a title with Oklahoma City the year before, making him one of the more unusual free-agent additions in the league this offseason.Philadelphia already added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James this summer, and Jones now joins a growing list of new faces chasing a championship the Sixers have not lifted in decades. He also reunites with Ariel Hukporti, his former Knicks teammate, giving Philadelphia two players who know exactly what it feels like to hoist a trophy.CategoryDetailsPlayerDillon JonesPrevious teamNew York KnicksNew teamPhiladelphia 76ersContract statusExhibit 10 deal (non-guaranteed training camp contract)Dillon Jones lands in the Philadelphia 76ers in an Exhibit 10 dealThe Sixers made the news official on Tuesday, announcing Dillon Jones' signing in a press release after ESPN's Dave McMenamin broke the news first. "Back-to-back champ Dillon Jones signed with the 76ers to an Exhibit 10 contract," McMenamin wrote, adding that Jones would join Philadelphia's training camp later this month.An Exhibit 10 deal carries no guarantees. It simply gives Philadelphia a low-risk window to evaluate Jones before deciding whether to convert him to a two-way contract or send him to the Delaware Blue Coats. For a player who has bounced through three organizations in two years, it is a familiar kind of audition.What adding Dillon Jones means for the Philadelphia 76ersJones gives Philadelphia size and versatility at forward, standing 6-foot-5 and 235 pounds with the strength to guard multiple positions. His NBA numbers do not jump off the page. Across 61 combined games with Oklahoma City and New York, he has averaged just 2.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.0 assist in under ten minutes a night.His G League work tells a different story. Jones averaged 15.2 points, 6.1 assists and 5.6 rebounds in 18 games for the Westchester Knicks last season, shooting close to 38 percent from three after making just 27.5 percent the year before. This kind of jump is exactly what earned him a senior-year MVP award in the Big Sky Conference, where he averaged 20.8 points, 10.1 rebounds and 5.2 assists at Weber State.If that shooting holds up, Philadelphia may have found a legitimate developmental piece buried inside a camp contract.Inside Dillon Jones' remarkable run to two championshipsJones barely played in either title run, appearing in just seven games and 39 minutes for the Knicks and none of them in the playoffs. Coach Mike Brown still leaned on him during the postseason. "I spoke to Dillon often during this playoff run," Brown said on The Roommates Show, explaining that Jones had just gone through a similar run with Oklahoma City.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: LSU leaves former pro-athletes off final roster, one night before SEC takes Lane Kiffin and Tigers to court
articles.summary: The LSU Tigers finalized their 105-player roster without former Ole Miss players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris amid the ongoing SEC lawsuit.
articles.body: One night before the SEC is scheduled to ask a federal judge in Alabama for a temporary restraining order, LSU has finalized its roster for the upcoming season. After nearly three weeks of court appearances involving multiple athletes in the Louisiana case, including former Ole Miss players Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, the Tigers decided not to add either player to its roster at any point this season. On Tuesday night, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin finalized the roster by adding Gabriel Reliford and Aidan Anding, bringing the Tigers to the 105-player limit. SEC ACCUSES LSU OF LETTING LANE KIFFIN RUN WILD AS EXPULSION VOTE COULD BE COMING THURSDAY IN EXPLOSIVE COURT FILING LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN The decision comes after Wright and Harris amended their complaints in district court to add the SEC as a defendant. A judge granted the players an injunction last week following a 12-hour hearing that featured SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey testifying in front of a packed courtroom in Baton Rouge. The SEC filed their own lawsuit, but in federal court against the Tigers Not even ten minutes into his testimony, there was a rumbling within the courtroom as word started to spread that the SEC had filed its own lawsuit against LSU, Lane Kiffin, AD Verge Ausberry and other members of the Tigers athletic department. "Did you authorize the SEC to sue LSU and coach Lane Kiffin?" attorney Tony Clayton asked Sankey. When asked why the conference took that step, Sankey pointed to the authority of the presidents and chancellors he represents. Inside a Louisiana Courtroom: SEC-LSU Legal Circus Played Out Like a John Grisham Novel in Stunning Showdown "We established our First Amendment right for freedom of association, so that our conference can make decisions and our members can make decisions about membership," Sankey said. Now, five days after the injunction was granted, with school officials releasing a roster on Friday night before this past weekend's game against Clemson that did not include both football players involved in the lawsuit, LSU has made its final decision. But, even with this decision made by the Tigers athletic department, there is still a scheduled hearing on Wednesday inside a Birmingham federal court, where the SEC is seeking a temporary restraining order that would allow the conference to enforce rules pertaining to pro-athletes making a return to college athletics. In addition to seeking the ability to enforce its rules, this TRO could also grant the SEC cover when it comes to penalizing LSU for actions related to this entire ordeal. "Today, the Southeastern Conference, headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama, filed a request for a temporary restraining order in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Alabama to protect the right of the Conference and its member institutions to govern themselves," the SEC said in a statement. "The SEC and its member universities have the right to establish, through agreed-upon governance procedures, the rules under which they voluntarily compete and to expect those rules to be followed," the SEC noted. "A commitment to those rules, and to the core principles of the Southeastern Conference, is an essential element of SEC membership. "Today’s filing is necessary to defend that right and preserve the Conference’s ability to govern competition among its members." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Lane Kiffin desperately tried to add former Ole Miss players In the early morning hours of Sunday, following LSU's 51-10 win over Clemson, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin spoke about the tough decision to not add those two players to his roster, touching on his relationship with Dae'Quan Wright that dates back to Ole Miss. "I'm just glad we played the way we did. Because I get it, even if we won close and ugly, the whole story would have been, 'Man, I screwed the team up by doing this," Kiffin noted. "I've been criticized heavily the last two weeks and I get that. I understand that. But my job is not to please you and worry about what you're going to write. My job is what I believe is right, and I believe we were fighting for what was right for those kids. "I'm not going to get into all the reasons, but that's what I believe. Maybe people don't like that, but they don't understand that. Maybe if they knew my relationship with Dae'Quan [Wright] they would." Kiffin has mentioned that when he was leaving Ole Miss for LSU, it was Dae'Quan Wright who stood up in the Rebels team gathering and told his teammates that he wanted Lane to lead the team through their CFP run. COLLEGE ATHLETICS' LATEST MESS: COURT ORDERS SAY PRO ATHLETES CAN PLAY, BUT SEC AND BIG TEN READY TO FIGHT In their filing on Tuesday, the SEC made a number of accusations against LSU for their handling of this entire matter, claiming that nobody at LSU can control head coach Lane Kiffin. "Expressed great concern that Defendants [President Wade] Rousse and [Athletic Director Verge] Ausberry have no meaningful control over Defendant Kiffin or the football program at LSU ... The consensus at the September 4 meeting was and continues to be that LSU’s demonstrated lack of institutional control at the University level—including complete lack of control over Defendant Kiffin’s actions." She said she wants Herro to have a relationship with their children, but also asked the court to put temporary and permanent safeguards in place. Henry referred to Herro’s "historical conduct" without detailing the conduct, saying she had "intentionally omitted" those details out of respect for him. Her claims are part of an ongoing legal case and have not been established as facts by a court.Tyler Herro’s ex-girlfriend Katya Henry seeks custody and child support in legal battleAccording to TMZ, Tyler Herro and Katya Henry filed separate lawsuits following their breakup, creating a legal dispute over custody and support."NBA star Tyler Herro and his baby mama Katya Henry have split, and it's already getting nasty ... the exes are duking it out in court over custody and support after their bitter breakup, TMZ has learned," the outlet reported.TMZ reported that the outlet obtained filings from both sides. Herro’s initial case asked the court to create a parenting schedule and determine the amount he should pay in child support. The Milwaukee Bucks star also said he had been voluntarily supporting Henry since she gave birth.Herro later dismissed his case.Henry then filed her own petition, saying she had been in a romantic relationship with Herro for nearly seven years. She described herself as the children’s primary caregiver and said she had handled most of the decisions involving them.Her request for primary custody is paired with a significant qualification. Henry said she wants their children to see their father, but believes certain safeguards are needed because of what she described as Herro’s "historical conduct."She asked for "safeguards and parameters should be implemented on a temporary and permanent basis in order to ensure the safety and well-being" of the children.The filing does not publicly detail the conduct Henry referenced in the material provided. Henry said there is a large difference between their incomes because Herro is a professional athlete who earns substantial money.Herro, 26, recently moved to Milwaukee after joining the Bucks as part of a trade package. He is also playing under a $33 million expiring contract, according to the information provided. His career earnings have already crossed $100 million, making finances an important factor in the child support discussion.The couple’s children are Zya Elise Herro, born September 14, 2021, and Harlem Herro, born January 12, 2023. Herro and Henry first became publicly linked after Herro pursued her on X during the 2020 pandemic.Their relationship has now ended. The case is still ongoing. More information could emerge as the court process moves forward, but for now, the filings offer only the competing positions of the two parents. articles.title: A's Top Pitching Prospect Jamie Arnold Taken to Hospital After Early Exit
articles.summary: In just his second start with Triple-A Las Vegas, A's top pitching prospect Jamie Arnold was struck in the head by a comebacker.
articles.body:
On Tuesday afternoon it was reported that the A's top prospect, Leo De Vries, would be undergoing surgery in the next few days, with an expected recovery time of up to eight months.

On Wednesday evening in Triple-A Las Vegas, the third batter of the game hit a Jamie Arnold sweeper 107.3 mph off the bat that drilled the A's lefty in the head. He stayed standing, but immediately walked over to the Aviators dugout. Arnold is the A's top pitching prospect, and the No. 57 prospect in MLB.

The A's later said that Arnold was taken to the hospital by the team's medical staff following this play, and another update will be provided by the organization when one is available.

Arnold was promoted to Triple-A last week , making his first appearance with Las Vegas on September 1. The lefty went five scoreless innings, giving up four hits and two walks, while striking out five.

He's also been on a tear in the second half of the season, going 5-0 and holding a 1.99 ERA across 11 starts spanning 54 ⅓ innings. In the first half, he'd held a 4.64 ERA in 13 starts spanning 64 innings.

He recently said that part of the difference for him had been relying on his changeup a bit more after the break, which had been leading to improved results — and a promotion.

There was some hope that De Vries would be able to help the Athletics in some fashion during the 2027 campaign, and this injury could put that into some doubt if the season begins on time.

Not only would he be back on the field around May if he's out for eight months, but he would still need to get up to speed in the minors before ultimately reaching the A's roster.

The same rings true for Arnold, though his situation is obviously different. First and foremost, the hope is that the left-hander is ok.

With that baseline health, there may not be a ton of difference for Arnold's trajectory to the big leagues. In fact, the lockout could end up serving him well.

If the MLB season ends up missing some games, that would mean a later start to the season. The MiLB campaign is still scheduled to take place, regardless of what is going on with the lockout negotiations, which means that Arnold and other non-40-man guys would be able to play ball.

The Las Vegas Aviators' schedule is set to begin on March 26 in Tacoma. If he's off to a hot start and the MLB season doesn't begin until May, there is a chance he could be in the A's rotation on Opening Day.

articles.title: "Esta generación va a marcar una época en el baloncesto español"
articles.standfirst: Las selecciones masculina y femenina tienen una cita con la historia en el Mundial de Ottawa. La primera llega como campeona de Europa pero nunca ha subido al podio mundial
articles.summary: Las selecciones masculina y femenina tienen una cita con la historia en el Mundial de Ottawa. La primera llega como campeona de Europa pero nunca ha subido al podio mundial
articles.body: España quiere hacer historia y no es una frase hecha. Las selecciones masculina y femenina de baloncesto paralímpico, ambas en pleno relevo generacional, llegan en un gran momento al Mundial de Ottawa (Canadá) que se disputa desde hoy al 19 de septiembre. Ellos como vigentes campeones europeos y ellas como bronce continental, pero sobre todo con la sensación de haberse asentado en la élite mundial y de poder competir de tú a tú a cualquiera, sea Estados Unidos o Gran Bretaña en el caso de la masculina o ante Países Bajos y EE.UU., en la femenina. Históricamente a España se le ha resistido el podio mundial. En Canadá quiere derribar un nuevo muro del deporte nacional. "Estamos muy ilusionados, pero también con la responsabilidad de saber que somos los actuales campeones de Europa y que todo lo que no sea estar entre los favoritos y pelear por las medallas supone no alcanzar el objetivo. España con los Mundiales no tiene una historia de amor muy bonita, siempre nos hemos quedado a las puertas de las medallas. Pero este equipo tiene mucha hambre de ganar. Va a ser una generación que va a marcar una época en el baloncesto español", asegura convencido Abraham Carrión, el seleccionador español y nuevo director técnico de Baloncesto en Silla de Ruedas en la FEDDF. El Mundial masculino lo disputan 16 selecciones y España ha quedado encuadrada en el Grupo C, "duro y competitivo" en palabras del seleccionador. Debuta hoy ante Colombia (15:30 horas), un combinado muy agresivo al contraataque. El siguiente duelo será ante Polonia el 11 de septiembre a las 20:45, una selección que apenas ha cambiado en la última década y a la que conocen bien. Y el último partido de la fase de grupos será el 12 ante Japón a las 1:15 (hora española), un equipo muy versátil y rápido que obligará a España a estar al cien por cien para no cometer errores pero al que el equipo de Carrión es superior en el juego interior. Todos los partidos de España, tanto de la selección española masculina como femenina, se emitirán desde la fase de grupos en RTVE Play, con narración en castellano, y algunos de ellos, sobre todo a partir de la segunda fase, también tendrán cabida en Teledeporte. Estados Unidos, Italia, Brasil y Países Bajos componen el Grupo A. Australia, Gran Bretaña, Turquía y Argentina, el B. Y Marruecos, Alemania, Irán y Canadá integran el D. La selección española se caracteriza por un juego muy rápido y vertical, que parte desde la defensa. Carrión apuesta por dificultar el ataque de los rivales para poder hacer transiciones y llevar a cabo un ataque rápido. “El objetivo en Ottawa es ser muy competitivos y aspirar a lo máximo. Luego pasarán cosas que no podremos controlar, pero cada vez que salimos a la pista somos conscientes de que somos uno de los rivales a batir", dice Carrión. Y más después del oro en Sarajevo el año pasado. “Esa medalla ha cambiado un poquito la forma en la que nos miran los rivales. Ganar un año no significa nada. Está muy bien, pero por mucho que hayamos conseguido tenemos que seguir demostrando quiénes somos. Queremos seguir haciendo historia y alcanzando podios”, dice con ambición Óscar Onrubia, que en 2025 fue elegido en el quinteto ideal del Europeo y es uno de los líderes de la renovación generacional. “En el Mundial tenemos que enfrentarnos a todos los rivales como si fuera el último partido de nuestra vida y dar el cien por cien. Así llegarán los resultados”, señala como fórmula para el éxito. “No estamos a menos nivel que Estados Unidos, Canadá o Gran Bretaña. Simplemente tenemos que ser un poco más constantes y sacar ese ADN que nos identifica. No creo que este equipo esté por debajo de ninguna otra selección”, añade. Un ADN que ya llevó a España a lograr la plata en los Juegos Paralímpicos de Río 2016. Pablo Zarzuela es uno de los pocos jugadores que vivió aquel momento histórico en la pista y que sigue en la selección. A sus 39 años, el andaluz mantiene intacta su ambición. “Seguir formando parte de la selección es un sueño, algo que me sigue manteniendo vivo y me genera mucha motivación porque siempre son objetivos nuevos. Nunca he llegado a una final en un Mundial y es un reto impresionante para ir acabando mi carrera”, dice Zarzuela. El jerezano, el jugador más veterano de la selección, apuesta por mantener la esencia del equipo, la humildad y los pies en el suelo. “Sabemos lo que nos ha llevado al éxito, lo tenemos dentro y hay que seguir manteniéndolo”, explica. Porque él ha vivido la cara y la cruz del deporte. De la plata en Río a caer en cuartos en París 2024. “Desde los últimos Juegos la selección ha cambiado muchísimo. El hambre que tenemos ahora por competir cada minuto es algo que no he visto en algún equipo. Somos ambiciosos y damos el cien por cien en todos los entrenamientos, en cada sesión de tiro, de gimnasio o de grupos. Y la química que tenemos dentro del equipo es algo que envidiaría cualquier quinteto del mundo. Y creo que eso es lo que nos va a llevar al podio”, dice con convicción ‘Pincho’ Ortega, que a sus 25 años es ya capitán de la selección y el jugador franquicia del equipo. “El baloncesto es un deporte de equipo, por mucho que yo lo haga bien si el equipo no está remando en la misma dirección, no vamos a llegar a nada”, dice restándose mérito antes de afrontar su segundo Mundial. En Hamburgo 2018 fue uno de los ‘rookies’. España se ha conjurado para cambiar la historia. “Esta selección puede llegar en Ottawa a donde quiera. Tiene un potencial enorme y mucho talento”, dice Zarzuela convencido. “Queremos demostrar que el oro europeo no fue casualidad. Vamos con presión pero es positivo”, añade Carrión.

articles.summary: "La creatividad inigualable y el compromiso con la excelencia de Phil Jackson restauraron nuestro legado de campeones, aportando cinco títulos"
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers homenajearán a Phil Jackson, que ganó cinco de sus 11 títulos de entrenador en la NBA con la franquicia californiana, con una estatua la próxima temporada. La estatua será de Phil Jackson, que será realizada por a Omri Amrany del estudio Rotblatt Amrany, se inaugurará el 9 de abril de 2027, antes del partido de los Lakers contra los Minnesota Timberwolves. Jeanie Buss, gobernadora interina de los Lakers y antigua pareja sentimental del exentrenador de 80 años (salieron durante 17 años y rompieron por una importante decisión de la NBA), fue la encargada de comunicar que Phil Jackson acompañará a Jerry West, Magic Johnson, Kobe Bryant (tiene dos estatuas), Shaquille O'Neal, Elgin Baylor, Pat Riley (entrenador), Chick Hearn (locutor) y Kareem Abdul-Jabbar como las leyendas de los Lakers con estatúa en el Crypto Center. "Phil Jackson es sinónimo de baloncesto ganador por una buena razón. Su magistral enfoque como entrenador sacó lo mejor de algunos de los jugadores más grandes que jamás hayan practicado este deporte. Tras aceptar la invitación de mi padre para unirse a los Lakers, la creatividad inigualable y el compromiso con la excelencia de Phil restauraron nuestro legado de campeones, aportando cinco títulos y estableciendo un estándar de excelencia para las generaciones venideras. Es una gran alegría poder conmemorar ese logro con la estatua que él tan merecidamente se ha ganado", compartió Jeanie Buss. Phil Jackson, uno de los 15 mejores entrenadores en la historia de la NBA, entrenó a los Lakers durante 11 temporadas repartidas en dos etapas (1999-2004 y 2005-11). Ganó tres anillos de la NBA con Kobe Bryant y Shaquille O'Neal como pilares, y otros dos Bryant y Pau Gasol como referentes.
