articles.title: Predicting the NBA's Top 5 MVP Candidates In 5 Years
articles.summary: The days of LeBron James, Stephen Curry, and Kevin Durant winning MVP trophies are behind us. Flash forward five years, and even the likes of Nikola Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and Luka Doncic will likely have aged out of the MVP race.
articles.body:
The days of LeBron James, Stephen Curry, and Kevin Durant winning MVP trophies are behind us. Flash forward five years, and even the likes of Nikola Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and Luka Doncic will likely have aged out of the MVP race.

The NBA is rapidly changing, and the old guard is slowly aging out, while a new crop of young talent has risen to take their spots.

Two quick caveats while predicting the field:

Let's assume good health for everyone on this list.

No players from the current rookie class qualify before seeing them in action.

Here is a look at five potential MVP candidates, five years down the road.

This one is fairly obvious. The NBA needs to be ready for Wembanyama to contend for MVP over the next eight to ten years. He just finished third in MVP voting this past season in his third campaign, was the unanimous Defensive Player of the Year, and is only scratching the surface of just how good he is going to be.

Looking back at last season's numbers, Wembanyama was a force on both ends of the floor. He averaged 25 points on 51.2/34.9/82.7 percent shooting splits while grabbing 11.5 rebounds and swatting away 3.1 shots per game. The Spurs had a 17 net rating while he was on the floor. He led these young Spurs to the Finals in his first postseason.

What the rest of the NBA should be concerned about is that Wembanyama is only 22 years old and just getting started. He hasn't even found his consistent spot on the floor where he can operate and dominate, like Dirk Nowitzki would work the high post.

In a few years, the NBA world may be looking at Wembanyama as the best player on the planet.

The No. 1 pick in the 2020 NBA Draft, Anthony Edwards has lived up to the hype. He already has big moments under his belt in both the regular season and the playoffs. In six seasons, Edwards has made two All-NBA teams, two Western Conference Finals, and has led the Timberwolves back to relevance.

Since Edwards' rookie season, his game has grown exponentially. First look at his three-point percentage: As a rookie, he shot 32.9 percent , and last season, he connected at a 39.9 percent clip. He evolved as a scorer into a legitimate playmaker for his teammates, even though his assist numbers have dipped the last two seasons from his career high of 5.1 assists in the 23-24 season.

The dip has more to do with teams playing more aggressively in their doubles on Edwards, which leads him to give up the ball early in possessions. With LaMelo Ball as his teammate, teams will not be able to double him as immediately as before.

Edwards is a multi-tool player, operating as a playmaker, a three-level scorer, and a post scorer. On top of all that, he's an elite defender.

A season is coming when it all comes together. Five years from now, Edwards will be turning 30 and at the peak of his powers.

It was just two seasons ago that Cade Cunningham finally broke out for the Detroit Pistons. There were flashes along the way, but Cunningham has been able to put it all together and just finished fifth in the MVP vote this past season.

Two seasons ago, Cunningham averaged a career-high 26.1 points; last season, his scoring dipped slightly, but he averaged 9.9 assists a night.

Cunningham is coming into his own as a do-it-all ball player. He has been everything for the Pistons, as they went from a great turnaround story to last year's 60-win team. He cranked up his scoring during the last playoff, aided by shooting 40.2 percent from three on 7.3 attempts.

That type of shooting is what Cunningham needs to bring with him to the regular season. He's a career 34 percent three-point shooter, and that will need to climb. Doing all this while maintaining a nearly double-digit assist average should put him in a position to be an MVP candidate, and five years from now, he will be right in his prime years.

Coming off winning Rookie of the Year, Cooper Flagg in five years' time might be a true force for the NBA world to have to deal with. He'll be just 24 years old and just entering his prime. That should put him squarely in the range of being an MVP contender.

The last 15 games of Flagg's rookie season should be used as the blueprint for ascent. During that stretch, he averaged 24.7 points , 6.8 rebounds, and 5.3 assists while coming up with 1.5 steals and 1.1 blocks per night. That is two-way excellence that also creates opportunities for his teammates. He has all the tools to be a multifaceted player who can lead a franchise.

Of course, after one season, there are areas that need work. He shot just 29.5 percent from three on 3.5 attempts for the year. The mechanics of his shot, though, are fine, and at Duke, he shot 38.5 percent from three.

Flagg should be a better three-point shooter going forward than he was in his rookie season. It should make his play even more deadly going forward.

This is a long-shot bid, but stay with me as I present my case.

Dylan Harper's numbers from his rookie season are not eye-popping: 11.8 points , 3.9 assists, 3.4 rebounds on 50.5/34.3/75.6 shooting splits in just 22.6 minutes a game off the bench.

The numbers don't dazzle, but Harper's game does.

With a litany of guards in San Antonio, Harper came off the bench last season but provided the Spurs with an all-important punch. He gets to the rim at ease, and, more impressively, he was able to do it in the playoffs against some of the toughest perimeter defenders in the NBA right now. He was the best Spurs guard in the Finals; he averaged 18 points and 6.4 rebounds per game; and he did not shrink under the spotlight.

The elephant in the room, of course, is that Harper is teammates with Wembanyama. That will make it more difficult for him to get votes.

Teammates both getting recognized as potential MVPs, has that ever happened? Inde ed, it has. Russell Westbrook and Kevin Durant finished fourth and fifth in MVP voting for the 2015-16 season.

That said, there is still a lot that has to go right for Harper in the next five seasons. Obviously, he needs to be a starter. If that isn't happening by the 2030-31 season, something has gone seriously wrong.

After that, he needs to keep improving his game, especially his three-point shooting.

Harper has the chance to be a truly special player, is already a key contributor on an NBA Finals team, and his role will only grow as he develops.

That growth might put him into MVP contention five seasons from now when he enters his prime.

Mo Dakhil spent six years with the Los Angeles Clippers and two years with the San Antonio Spurs as a video coordinator, as well as three years with the Australian men's national team. Follow him on X, @MoDakhil_NBA .

articles.body: Dos partidos de pretemporada han servido para que Ignas Brazdeikis se convierta en uno de los primeros nombres propios del nuevo Unicaja de Txus Vidorreta. El lituano ha aprovechado sus primeras oportunidades para dejar muy buenas sensaciones y empezar a justificar la apuesta del club malagueño. Su llegada a Málaga no generó demasiado ruido, pero su experiencia en la NBA, el Zalgiris o el Olympiacos hacía pensar que podía ser un jugador importante si recuperaba su mejor nivel. Todavía es pronto y los rivales tampoco permiten sacar conclusiones definitivas. La próxima semana, ante La Laguna Tenerife y el Real Madrid en el Torneo Costa del Sol, llegará una prueba mucho más seria. articles.body:
Caitlin Clark closed out the group phase of the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup on a relative high as the United States sailed past Czechia.

Through three games in the tournament, Clark is Team USA's leader in assists and fifth in scoring while playing more minutes than anybody else.

USA's next World Cup opponent and game time set

Caitlin Clark sets unwanted personal record in FIBA World Cup

The United States already had a quarterfinal spot secured when it took the floor against Czechia on Monday. That allowed coach Kara Lawson to ease the workload on her starters a bit and utilize her entire bench.

Clark wound up playing 22 minutes, scoring nine points and dishing out seven assists.

The Indiana Fever guard has been solid in her first major tournament for the senior national team. She opened with a double-double but has since leveled off a bit.

The regression was to be expected. The international game presents a different test to what WNBA players are familiar with, and it's tough for any one star to stand out on a team with as much talent as the United States.

Nobody expected the U.S. to have as much trouble as it did against Italy, so Hungary shouldn't be overlooked. The Hungarians are 19th in the FIBA ranking , though, and got blown out by 46 points against France in the group phase.

Assuming the United States advances, a matchup with Spain or Australia could await. Spain has already punched its ticket to the last eight, with Australia playing Italy on Wednesday.

articles.title: Antetokounmpo ya tiene hogar en Miami: una mansión de 13,5 millones de dólares
articles.standfirst: Tiene un terreno de una hectárea, 1.100 metros cuadrados construidos, ocho dormitorios, 10 baños...
articles.summary: Tiene un terreno de una hectárea, 1.100 metros cuadrados construidos, ocho dormitorios, 10 baños...
articles.body: La llegada de Giannis Antetokounmpo a los Heat ha sido una de las grandes operaciones del mercado NBA. El alero, tras estar toda su carrera NBA en Milwaukee, comenzará una nueva vida en Miami y ya tiene vivienda. No una cualquiera, sino una mansión por la que ha pagado 13,5 millones de dólares. El nuevo hogar de la estrella griega se encuentra en el exclusivo vecindario de Pinecrest, donde suelen residir otros jugadores de los Heat. Tyler Herro vivía ahí hasta que fue incluido en la operación de Antetokounmpo y puso su casa a la venta. También Jimmy Butler tuvo su hogar en el barrio. La mansión de Antetokounmpo tiene unos 1.100 metros cuadrados construidos y cuenta con ocho dormitorios, 10 baños completos, dos aseos, una sala multimedia, piscina, jacuzzi y una casa de huéspedes. El terreno en el que está construida es de cerca de una hectárea y lo único de lo que no dispone es de acceso directo al mar. Es la cuarta propiedad que el jugador griego compra en lo que va de año, pero la única en la que va a residir. Previamente había adquirido inmuebles multifamiliares en Wisconsin, Chicago y Brooklyn por valor de 69 millones de dólares. Con esa última y en mitad del ruido sobre su salida de los Bucks, los aficionados de los Nets y los Knicks llegaron a ilusionarse con su llegada, aunque sólo se trataba de inversiones.

articles.title: WNBA Fans Have A Field Day As Fever Rookie Johnson Interviews Herself
articles.summary: Raven Johnson’s self-interview is a masterclass in controlling your own narrative.
articles.body:
Who said rookies can't be media savvy? Because Indiana Fever 's Raven Johnson just proved everyone wrong when she recently took over her own media session after a team practice. And fans are absolutely loving it!

It's been all about Team USA stars Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston ever since the WNBA season paused for the 2026 FIBA World Cup. As the duo prepares to take on Hungary in Berlin, Germany, in the quarterfinals, the Fever stars have already returned to practice. Rookie Johnson felt this was her time to shine.

Johnson, who was made available to the media after Tuesday's practice, gave the press a crash course by guessing what their questions for her might be! When asked (jokingly) whether she wanted to suggest what reporters should ask her, she used the opportunity to interview herself, asking a few questions about her week off (she traveled to Seattle ) and the current World Cup.

The Fever rookie kicked off her self-interview with the first question: "Raven, how do you feel coming back from the break and working out?"

Answering her own question about returning from the WNBA break, Johnson cheekily said, "Oh, we've been back, guys. We've been in the gym for three days, and everybody looks locked in and ready to make a good playoff run."

The 23-year-old rookie guard fired off another question to herself: "Raven, have you been watching the FIBA Cup, Caitlin and Aliyah?"

"Yes, I've been watching it. Shout out to my girls. They're killing it. And they're definitely going to walk away with the gold medal," Johnson answered again to herself.

Clearly having fun by taking control of her own media session, Johnson posed her third question: "Raven, why are you always smiling?"

The five-foot-nine guard finished her quick-fire round with a big grin across her face, adding, "I'm smiling because I love it here and I'm always smiling because that's just who I am."

As much as the bit cracked every reporter in the room, it looks like fans online loved Johnson's nonchalant attitude through and through.

Responding to the clip shared by an Indianapolis-based sports reporter on X (formerly Twitter), a fan wrote, "Hope you guys gave her your salary for the day. One woman show right there."

Applauding the University of South Carolina graduate for her effort, another fan quipped, "Columbia local media has trained her so well 😂"

A third fan summarized the whole scene, writing, "Raven really said, "I got this one" 😭."

A fourth user also joked, "Since ABC left for FIBA Raven Johnson has taken control of the media and established a dictatorship of the proletariat in Indiana generational run."

Indiana chose Johnson with the 10th overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft. She has a stellar reputation as a defensive player and a history of college championships.

Although she made a good impression throughout preseason and training camp, she is still getting used to the professional ranks. As veteran Ty Harris settled into the team and recovered fully from the injury she sustained the season before, Johnson slipped out of the rotation. She is averaging 10.3 minutes, 3.1 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.2 assists per game.

Johnson finds herself struggling with shooting, as she only makes 40 percent of her shots from the field and 24 percent of her three-pointers. She is only a rookie, of course, but her length and athleticism allow her to affect the game, especially on defense.

Although Johnson's talent is highly regarded by the Indiana coaching staff, her professional growth is still in its infancy. In her rookie season, Johnson is "comfortable" with where she is now. She continues to pick things up "really fast" and is "off the rip now."

articles.title: Malik Beasley Makes Unusual Travel Request Amid Federal Case
articles.summary: Malik Beasley is trying to keep parts of his normal life moving while his future remains tied to a federal case. The former NBA guard has asked a judge to gi...
articles.body:
Malik Beasley is trying to keep parts of his normal life moving while his future remains tied to a federal case. The former NBA guard has asked a judge to give him more freedom to travel during a brief window in September.

The request comes as Beasley faces strict conditions following his arrest. What makes it unusual is where he wants to go and why.

Malik Beasley Wants To Travel For Family And Work

According to court documents obtained by TMZ Sports , Beasley asked for permission to travel from September 6 through September 15. His proposed stops include Rancho Mirage and Beverly Hills in California, before a work trip to Hawaii.

The California portion is personal. Beasley wants to spend time with his two young children before they return to school, while the Hawaii portion involves a resort promotion connected to his social media work.

His legal team also offered several safeguards as part of the request. Beasley would provide his full itinerary, remain reachable by phone and return to Miami after the trip, according to the filing. Prosecutors do not oppose the request.

That does not mean the court has approved the trip. The request covers a period that began September 6, so the timing could also leave part of the proposed travel window unresolved.

Malik Beasley Remains Under Tight Court Restrictions

The request arrives only months after federal prosecutors charged Beasley in a case involving alleged manipulation of NBA performances for betting purposes. The Justice Department says Beasley and five others were charged in June over an alleged scheme involving sports bribery, illegal betting and money laundering.

Prosecutors allege that Beasley agreed to manipulate his performance in NBA games and provided information that could help others place bets. The government has described the conduct as an effort to turn his NBA performance into a source of illegal betting profit.

An FBI official summarized the allegation in blunt terms, saying Beasley "allowed himself to be bought." The statement reflects the government's accusation, not a finding of guilt.

Beasley has denied the allegations through his legal defense and pleaded not guilty in July. He was released on a $100,000 bond, with conditions that include restrictions related to gambling and contact with people connected to the case.

The Hawaii trip matters because it shows Beasley is trying to keep working while his case plays out. His lawyer said that he has a job on social media. This gives him a clear reason to travel for work, not just for personal reasons.

This creates a tricky situation for Beasley. With his basketball career paused, his travel limited, and a legal battle looming, he's just trying to balance his court-ordered restrictions with his desire to stay connected to his family and keep working.

For now, Beasley's request is only a request. The federal case continues, and any travel approval would come with the restrictions already attached to his release.

articles.title: “You Were Gutless” – Former Indiana Coach Slams Cathy Engelbert After Retirement Announcement
articles.summary: Cathy Engelbert’s retirement announcement has stirred up the WNBA world. As the league begins its search for a new leader, experts are slamming her over mult...
articles.body:
Cathy Engelbert 's retirement announcement has stirred up the WNBA world. As the league begins its search for a new leader, experts are slamming her over multiple controversies. The most recent addition is the former Indiana University Hoosiers interim head coach Dan Dakich.

In a recent YouTube video , Dakich discussed Engelbert's retirement announcement and comments from NBA Commissioner Adam Silver.

Adam Silver praised Engelbert's contributions to the league in his statement. The NBA commissioner said that the 61-year-old was part of the "most significant period of growth in the league's 30-year history." However, Dakich disagreed with Silver's assessment.

"I'll give you two words, Caitlin Clark . That's it. Ain't no more. You held the league back, lady. You were gutless. You've made that league a laughing stock," Dakich said.

The former Indiana University Hoosiers interim coach bluntly described Engelbert as "the worst commissioner in the history of professional sports." Dakich criticized Engelbert's stance on transgender athletes in women's sports.

"See, the W in WNBA stands for women. But Cathy Engelbert and her ilk [kind] can't actually define what a woman is. And that's a problem that ultimately caught up to her hate," Dakich said.

Slamming her further, Dakich added, "Are you nuts, lady? You're 61 years old, and you can't define what a woman is publicly because you're a coward. You are gutless. You are spineless. And now you are out."

Dan Dakich Believes Cathy Engelbert Was Unable To Handle Caitlin Clark

Clark's rise in basketball has been nothing short of astounding. The 2024 NCAA women's championship game featuring Clark drew more viewers than the men's final. When she entered the WNBA, the league's revenue model scaled up, while merchandise sales increased by 200% and the league garnered multi-million-dollar broadcast audiences.

Despite Caitlin Clark 's impact on the league, many experts believe Engelbert failed to advocate for her. Criticizing the WNBA commissioner, Dakich said

"Her retirement comes years after mounting controversies. Her inability to stand up for the golden goose, Caitlin Clark. It's been nothing but a train wreck. Players have mauled Clark out of jealousy. Fans ejected from games over well-later-disproven racist comments, which has been all b-lls–-t."

Cathy Engelbert will retire as WNBA commissioner at the end of this year, on December 31, 2026. Notably, reports have circulated that potential candidates are being shortlisted , and the search process could begin later this month.

articles.title: 76ers sign ex-Knicks $5M 2-time NBA champion to potentially team with LeBron James, Jaylen Brown
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers made an under the radar signing on Tuesday. The back-to-back NBA champion will have to play alongside LeBron James and the rest of the...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have struck gold this offseason, as they have quickly become one of the favorites to win the NBA championship. No one expected the offseason to go this way for Philadelphia after the team was eliminated in the second round of the playoffs last season.

However, it all started with a surprising move for Jaylen Brown . Brown's relationship with the Boston Celtics had reached a breaking point, allowing the 76ers to acquire the former NBA Finals MVP.

"Jaylen Brown has a new home, as the Boston Celtics agreed to send the former NBA Finals MVP to the Philadelphia 76ers in a blockbuster trade Wednesday, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The 76ers are sending Paul George , two first-round picks (2028, 2031) and two second-round selections (2028, 2030) to Boston to complete the deal, sources said," ESPN wrote.

The trade would then get the attention of four-time NBA champion LeBron James . The former MVP ultimately signed with Philadelphia, giving the 76ers another superstar to add to their championship-caliber roster.

"LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers for his final run at another NBA championship, he announced Friday," ESPN's Dave McMenamin wrote. "James, 41, is signing a two-year, $8 million contract with a player option, Klutch Sports Group CEO Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania."

The organization has also been making some smaller moves by signing players to Exhibit 10 contracts. On Tuesday, Philadelphia signed back-to-back NBA champion Dillon Jones to an Exhibit 10 contract.

"Back-to-back champ Dillon Jones signed with the 76ers to an Exhibit 10 contract, a team source told ESPN. He'll be a part of Philly's training camp later this month," ESPN's Dave McMenamin wrote.

Jones was selected in the first round of the 2024 NBA Draft by the Washington Wizards before his draft rights were sent to the Oklahoma City Thunder . He spent his rookie season with the Thunder and later joined the New York Knicks on a two-way contract.

The former first-rounder has made $5 million in his career. Jones has already won two NBA championships in his young career, doing so with the Thunder and Knicks in consecutive seasons. Now, he has another opportunity to join a championship contender in Philadelphia. If Jones can earn a two-way contract with the 76ers, he would legitimately have a chance to become an NBA champion in three consecutive seasons.

articles.title: Domantas Sabonis, Hornets Trade Rumors Addressed by Kings Insider After Report Surfaces
articles.summary: After a rumor surfaced online that the Charlotte Hornets are on the verge of completing a trade for Sacramento Kings veteran big man Domantas Sabonis, one expert quickly dismissed the idea.
articles.body:
After a rumor surfaced online that the Charlotte Hornets are on the verge of completing a trade for Sacramento Kings veteran big man Domantas Sabonis, one expert quickly dismissed the idea.

Kings insider Matt George of Sactown Sports 1140 shot down the rumor involving Sabonis and the Hornets as "not true or accurate," and he noted that Sacramento and Charlotte haven't engaged in trade discussions "since weeks before the NBA Draft."

Sabonis is coming off a lost season in which he was limited to a career-low 19 games due to knee surgery. He also chose not to participate in Lithuania's FIBA World Cup qualifying window as he eyes a return in the 2026-27 campaign.

The Hornets have already made massive changes over the offseason, trading star point guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves and veteran wing Miles Bridges to the Phoenix Suns. Charlotte hasn't made the playoffs since 2016, but a 44-38 finish last season has fueled optimism for a bright future.

Acquiring Sabonis would surely boost the Hornets' chances of ending their playoff drought, as the 10-year veteran is a double-double machine when healthy. But for now, it sounds like the Kings aren't in a rush to get rid of the three-time All-Star.

articles.title: Los tres mandamientos de Pedro Martínez en el Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: El técnico blanco explica las líneas maestras del juego que quiere que haga el equipo: "Defensa agresiva, jugar rápido y compartir el balón"
articles.summary: El técnico blanco explica las líneas maestras del juego que quiere que haga el equipo: "Defensa agresiva, jugar rápido y compartir el balón"
articles.body: Después de los dos primeros amistosos de pretemporada, el juego del Real Madrid se va pareciendo a lo que se ha visto en los últimos equipos que ha dirigido Pedro Martínez. En declaraciones a los medios del club blanco, el técnico a explicado las primeras líneas maestras de lo que desea: "Me gustaría que tuviéramos una defensa proactiva, que sea una defensa agresiva, que juguemos rápido y que seamos capaces de compartir el balón. Estas serían un poco las prioridades y los factores básicos que queremos que se vean lo más pronto posible". El nuevo entrenador madridista se estrenó con una derrota ante el Río Breogán (110-102) y el fin de semana pasada arrolló por 121-80 a un Kosner Baskonia en cuadro que apenas ha podido trabajar cinco contra cinco. Este jueves jugará la XV edición del Torneo Costa del Sol midiéndose primero a La Laguna Tenerife y este sábado al Unicaja. Serán sus últimos duelos de preparación antes de acometer la Supercopa de la Euroliga, donde el viernes 18 de septiembre se las verá en semifinales con el Dubái Basketball en el primer choque oficial del curso. Pedro Martínez, después de unas semanas de trabajo, valora muy positivamente "la actitud de los jugadores. Desde el primer día están intentando hacer las cosas con muy buena mentalidad, entrenando con muchísimo esfuerzo, sabiendo que es un momento muy importante para nosotros porque estamos sentando las bases de lo que luego vamos a querer hacer en la competición. La mentalidad de los jugadores me está pareciendo extraordinaria". Para el entrenador del Real Madrid es fundamental que "todos los jugadores estén en la misma página y que los entrenadores seamos capaces de tener claros cuáles son nuestras prioridades en ataque y en defensa. Y confiar en que el trabajo que hacemos para que esas prioridades sean importantes nos sirva en los partidos". Además, Martínez ensalza la labor de quienes llevan más tiempo en el equipo, que están tratando de que la adaptación de los nuevos, algunos sin experiencia en Euroliga, sea lo más rápido posible. "Los jugadores más experimentados están siendo un ejemplo en el día a día y están tirando del grupo de una forma encomiable. Contamos con ellos porque saben lo que significa llevar esta camiseta y también tienen la experiencia de jugar competiciones de altísimo nivel que son las que habitualmente juega el Real Madrid. Ellos están enseñando el camino a los nuevos, que lo tienen que aprender y que no tienen mucho tiempo para ello. Esa conjunción entre los jugadores más experimentados y los que llevan menos tiempo ahora mismo es de vital importancia", considera.

articles.title: NBA trade rumor:  Dallas Mavericks could bid farewell to $118.5 million 3x All-NBA Star to build new roster around Cooper Flagg
articles.summary: NBA News: Kyrie Irving hasn't played an NBA game in over a year, and he's already at the center of trade speculation. The Dallas Mavericks insist he's part of t.
articles.body: Kyrie Irving hasn't played an NBA game in over a year, and he's already at the center of trade speculation. The Dallas Mavericks insist he's part of their plans heading into the 2026-27 season, but the front office overhaul around him tells a more complicated story.New president Masai Ujiri and new head coach Dusty May inherited a roster stripped of familiar faces, with Anthony Davis and Klay Thompson already traded away. Irving, one of the last links to the Luka Doncic era, is now recovering from a torn ACL and walking into a franchise explicitly building around a 19-year-old. That combination is enough to keep his name in circulation before the trade deadline, even without a formal shopping effort.CategoryDetailPlayerKyrie IrvingCurrent TeamDallas MavericksContract Status3-year, $118.5 million extension (signed July 2025); includes 2027-28 player optionSalary Cap Hit$39,491,282 (2026-27)Trade LikelihoodNot imminent — Mavericks maintain they intend to keep himLatest Insider UpdateESPN's Tim MacMahon reports rival teams are monitoring his fitDallas Mavericks could move Kyrie Irving ahead of the trade deadlineKyrie Irving posted 25.5 points and 5.1 assists per game across his Mavericks tenure before tearing his ACL in the 2024-25 season, and he's set to make his return in the season opener on October 21 against the Houston Rockets. MacMahon reported that Irving "could be a prime target for contenders before the trade deadline" if Ujiri opens that door.As of now, however, Dallas has held firm. The front office has publicly committed to keeping Irving, even as the roster around him gets rebuilt from the ground up. Coach Dusty May, who takes over a team he didn't build, said flatly, "I couldn't be more excited to be on his team," pointing to Irving's preparation and shot-making as tools he wants to lean on early in the season.Dallas Mavericks looking to build around Cooper FlaggThe bigger story in Dallas isn't Irving's trade value; it's Flagg's development. The 2026 Rookie of the Year is the organizing principle for everything the Mavericks do now, and Irving has already taken on a mentorship role with him despite missing the entire season on the sidelines.Flagg credited Irving's guidance through a difficult rookie transition, saying, "I never lost that much in my life," about the adjustment to NBA-level competition. Dallas wants that relationship to continue, not end in a trade.Kyrie Irving's market could be a bit coldEven if Dallas struggles early and decides to explore the market, moving Irving won't be simple. He's 34, coming off a major knee injury, and there's no clear wave of teams with an urgent need at his position right now. Front offices are increasingly cautious about surrendering draft capital for older guards under the current cap rules, and Irving still has to prove he can perform at his previous level post-injury. Any deal Dallas makes is more likely to net a discounted return than a strong one.Irving's actual trade value won't be clear until he's back on the floor. articles.title: “We are also extremely proud that in spite of some criticism..”: How Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry taught their kids to embrace the spotlight without letting criticism define them
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have spent years raising their children while millions of people watch their family life from the outside. Riley became.
articles.body: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have spent years raising their children while millions of people watch their family life from the outside. Riley became a familiar face during Stephen’s NBA career when she was still a toddler, while Canon later found himself at the center of an unnecessary online debate about his weight. Through those moments, Stephen and Ayesha have tried to give their children something more valuable than protection from every comment: the confidence to remain themselves.That approach did not begin recently. Ayesha spoke openly about it in 2015, when Riley was just two years old, and Stephen has now offered a similar message as the couple raises four children. Their approach has evolved with their family, but the idea remains consistent: criticism may come with being a Curry, but it should not decide how their children grow up. Ayesha Curry stood by Riley when the spotlight brought criticismRiley first experienced the strange side of public attention during the 2015 NBA playoffs, when she joined her father at a press conference and quickly became the star of the room. Her playful personality won over plenty of fans, although some people questioned whether a child should have been part of such a high-profile media moment.Ayesha did not believe Riley needed to be hidden simply because cameras were present. In her June 4, 2015 TIME essay, “How to Parent When Your Kid Goes Viral”, she explained that she and Stephen wanted their daughter to enjoy her childhood even while their family dealt with the growing attention surrounding Stephen and the Golden State Warriors. “I believe you should let your children be children, and don’t be afraid to be a parent, regardless of who’s watching,” Ayesha wrote.She also addressed the criticism Riley received after appearing alongside Stephen, making it clear that the family did not view the moment as something they needed to regret. “We are also extremely proud that in spite of some criticism, Riley was able to share in that experience with her father and bring joy and laughter into the lives and homes of many all over the world,” Ayesha wrote in the same TIME article.More importantly, Ayesha explained that the family tried to preserve Riley’s ordinary routines even when Stephen’s professional life became hectic. She wrote that bedtime routines and daily activities remained in place, while Riley continued doing things she enjoyed, including horseback riding and swimming. For Ayesha, being present mattered more than allowing the noise around the family to dictate their parenting.She made that belief clear when she wrote, “You can never be too busy for your child.”That same instinct appeared again when criticism moved from Riley to her younger brother Canon.Stephen Curry wants his children to carry the Curry name with confidenceIn May 2019, when Canon was 10 months old, Ayesha shared a family photo after the Warriors defeated the Portland Trail Blazers in the Western Conference Finals. After someone asked whether she was pregnant again, she explained that her son weighed around 30 pounds and joked that he was “breaking my back in every Photo.” The conversation took an uglier turn when another commenter questioned Canon’s weight and suggested that the baby had serious health issues.Ayesha immediately pushed back with “Excuse you? No. Just no.” Her response showed the same boundary she had established with Riley: public attention did not give strangers permission to make personal judgments about her children.Seven years later, Stephen offered a look at the other side of that parenting equation. In a February 2026 interview with PEOPLE, he discussed raising Riley, Ryan, Canon and their youngest child, Caius, with Ayesha, describing parenting as “the best gift and responsibility” and explaining that he enjoys watching each child develop a distinct personality.Stephen also draws from his own upbringing as the son of former NBA player Dell Curry, explaining that he grew up with “support but also tough love” and wants to strike a similar balance with his own children.That philosophy becomes especially important because Stephen knows his children will always carry a famous surname. During the same PEOPLE interview, he explained the message he gives them: “They know what their last name is. I tell them not to shy away from it. Be confident in who you are… and have fun.”That advice brings the Curry family's parenting approach full circle. Ayesha has made it clear that her children should be allowed to enjoy ordinary childhood moments even when people criticize them, while Stephen wants them to understand that being a Curry is something they can embrace rather than something they need to hide.The couple cannot control every opinion that follows their family, but they can control how their children respond to it. For Stephen and Ayesha, that means stepping in when criticism crosses a line while giving their kids enough confidence to keep enjoying the spotlight on their own terms.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jalen Brunson to Host 'Saturday Night Live' Season 52 Premiere After Knicks' NBA Title
articles.summary: After leading the New York Knicks to the 2026 NBA championship, star point guard Jalen Brunson continues to reach new heights in his popularity.
articles.body:
After leading the New York Knicks to the 2026 NBA championship, star point guard Jalen Brunson continues to reach new heights in his popularity.

On Wednesday, Brunson was announced as the host of the season 52 premiere of Saturday Night Live on Sept. 26:

When Brunson takes the stage for the SNL season 52 premiere, he will be the first basketball player to host the show since LeBron James in 2007.

Brunson is known for having a dry personality in front of the cameras, so fans will surely enjoy seeing him open up a different side of himself during the long-running sketch comedy show. Since SNL is produced and shot in New York City, it's safe to assume that other members of the Knicks roster will be in attendance to watch their floor general host the show.

While Brunson typically prefers to present a stoic demeanor, his comedic chops can be seen on his Roommates Show podcast alongside Knicks wing Josh Hart. The Athletic's James L. Edwards III detailed an instance in which Brunson fired barbs at Hart for laughing after he said Steve Nash was his favorite point guard.

"Why was he your favorite?" Hart asked. "You didn't emulate him at all. … OK, so when did you stop passing?"

Brunson retorted: "When you were on my team."

"So you're saying you got to be a selfish player once you got to Villanova? That's why we didn't like you," Hart replied.

"That's why we won," Brunson responded in an argument-ending statement.

Fans will certainly be interested to see whether Hart or any other Knicks teammates join Brunson on stage when he hosts SNL as part of the continued celebration of New York's first NBA championship in 53 years.

articles.title: Rutgers men's basketball coach Steve Pikiell reveals cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Associate head coach Brandin Knight will be the team's interim coach when Pikiell is absent during the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
Rutgers men's basketball coach Steve Pikiell announced Wednesday that he was diagnosed with cancer earlier this year.

Pikiell did not reveal what type of cancer he has in a statement posted to Rutgers' website, but said that he had recently undergone "a successful surgery" and that he and doctors "have a kick-ass game plan to finish treatment." If and when Pikiell is unable to coach in 2026-27, assistant coach Brandin Knight will be the team's interim coach.

"I will still be involved with the team to the best of my ability as I navigate the challenges of the season through treatment," Pikiell's statement said. "I have great confidence in Coach Knight, the rest of the talent staff, and our exceptional student-athletes. I know they will do an amazing job leading our program when I'm not able to."

Pikiell has been Rutgers' basketball coach since arriving from Stony Brook ahead of the 2016-17 season. The Scarlet Knights went 14-20 in 2025-26 and are 161-160 overall in his time with the team.

In Pikiell's 10 seasons in charge, Rutgers has made the NCAA tournament twice. Those appearances came in 2021 and 2022.

Knight has been the team's associate head coach for the past five seasons and was hired as an assistant when Pikiell joined the team. The former Pitt guard was an assistant at his alma mater for eight seasons before joining Rutgers.

"Those of us who know Steve, know the determination and strength he brings to everything he does," Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn said. "I know he will bring that same spirit to every treatment and every day ahead. We are grateful to Coach Knight for his willingness to step up during this challenging time and to our entire staff for their great care and compassion for Coach and our student-athletes. There is no set timeline for Coach Pikiell's full return, but we look forward to the day when he is back on our sideline."

Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn said in a statement that there is "no set timeline for Coach Pikiell's full return."

The 58-year-old Pikiell is preparing to enter his 11th season as head coach at Rutgers.

He has compiled a 161-160 overall record and a 77-119 mark in Big Ten play with two trips to the NCAA tournament, one to the NIT and one to the CBC.

The Scarlet Knights made back-to-back trips to the NCAA tournament in 2021 and 2022, and they reached the Round of 32 in 2021.

Rutgers has not been back to the NCAA tourney since 2022, though, and it is coming off three consecutive losing seasons, going 15-17 in both 2023-24 and 2024-25, and 14-20 last season.

Prior to his time at Rutgers, Pikiell was the head coach for 11 seasons at Stony Brook, going 192-156 with one NCAA tourney berth, three NIT appearances and two CBI appearances.

For his career, Pikiell owns an overall record of 353-316 at the Division I level.

If Pikiell is unable to perform his duties at any time during the 2026-27 season, the reins will be handed to Knight, who played collegiately at the University of Pittsburgh and appeared in one NBA game for the Houston Rockets in 2004-05.

Knight was an assistant coach at Pitt from 2008 to 2016, and he has been an assistant at Rutgers since 2016, taking on the associate head coach role in 2021.

articles.title: MAJOR Update on LA Clippers Flipping Brandon Ingram To Recoup Picks Lost in Kawhi Leonard Investigation
articles.summary: A major update has emerged on the recent rumors that the Los Angeles Clippers could move Brandon Ingram in another […]
articles.body:
A major update has emerged on the recent rumors that the Los Angeles Clippers could move Brandon Ingram in another trade to try to get back some of the first-round picks they lost in the punishment from the Kawhi Leonard investigation.

Last week, the NBA revealed the Clippers' punishment following a year-long investigation into salary cap circumvention to win the Leonard free agent sweepstakes in 2019. And it was historic.

The Clippers will have to forfeit five future first-round picks. The franchise was fined $30 million. Owner Steve Ballmer is suspended from all league and team activities for a year. President of Business Operations Gillian Zucker is suspended without pay for a year, and President of Basketball Operations Lawrence Frank is suspended without pay for 6 months. Also, Leonard was hit with a $700,000 fine.

Will the Los Angeles Clippers trade Brandon Ingram?

The worst part of the punishment for the team and fans is losing five valuable first-rounders over the next half-decade. It is a penalty that many NBA analysts have considered a living death for five years. However, the organization could get some signs of life and offer hope if they were willing to move some of the assets they have to get some future first-round picks.

That is why Ingram's name has popped up in trade rumors despite the trade that is sending him from Toronto to LA for Leonard not even being completed yet. The two-time All-Star is right in his prime at 29 years old, and he has a player option for 2027-28 . For playoff contenders that see a lot of value in the 10-year veteran, they might be willing to part with one or two first-round picks for him.

However, according to NBA insider Jake Fischer, that's not going to happen. In a new Bleacher Report live stream, he said: "I've been given no indication that the Clippers are actively looking to move Brandon Ingram at this period."

Why the Los Angeles Clippers won't trade Brandon Ingram

The Clippers having no plans to flip Ingram isn't a surprise. Is this going to be a lost season for LA? Yes. Are they rebuilding? Yes. Could they use more first-rounders to help in that process? Absolutely. But they still need to play games next season and hopefully draw some fans to the Intuit Dome in the fall, winter, and spring.

If you move Ingram for picks, it leaves a lineup with Darius Garland and rookie Keaton Wagler as the best players. With that duo leading the way, the Clippers would be set up for a historically bad season. That would be a nightmare decision after what happened last week.

Ingram is not a superstar, but he is a pretty good player. He can easily put up All-Star numbers again next season and give LA fans something to watch. Plus, it takes pressure off Wagler and allows him to develop. Furthermore, Garland, as a second scoring option, is a better fit for him. They probably won't make the playoffs, but with a good coach like Tyronn Lue, maybe they can compete for a play-in spot this season.

In the lead up to his first training camp as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers, Jaylen Brown has offered some insight into his mindset as he thinks about his legacy in the NBA.

articles.title: NBA Draft Pick Trey Kaufman-Renn Granted TRO for Sixth Year of NCAA Eligibility
articles.summary: As college football is trying to navigate a situation with players drafted into the NFL coming back, college basketball has been thrust into the same situation with Minnesota Timberwolves draftee Trey Kaufman-Renn.
articles.body:
As college football is trying to navigate a situation with players drafted into the NFL coming back, college basketball has been thrust into the same situation with Minnesota Timberwolves draftee Trey Kaufman-Renn.

Per Nathan Baird of the Indianapolis Star , Kaufman-Renn has been granted a temporary restraining order against the NCAA that will make him eligible for a sixth year in college basketball.

Baird noted the judge's ruling means the NCAA can't deny Kaufman-Renn's "eligibility based on his five years in college and four years playing for the Boilermakers, or his professional status."

Kaufman-Renn, who was selected with the No. 59 overall pick by the Timberwolves in June's draft, filed a lawsuit in August seeking an additional year of college eligibility.

Even though Kaufman-Renn arrived at Purdue for the 2021-22 season, he redshirted and didn't appear in a game his first year. He did appear in 147 games for the Boilermakers over the next four seasons.

Under the NCAA's age-based eligibility rule , student-athletes who enter college no later than the academic year after their 19th birthday will have up to five years of eligibility.

Kaufman-Renn's argument was based around the rule and if it had been in place when he originally got to Purdue that he wouldn't have had to sit during his true freshman season.

Baird noted there is currently no set date for a preliminary injunction hearing.

It's unclear where Kaufman-Renn intends to play college basketball, assuming he remains eligible when the 2026-27 season begins. He wrote on his Instagram Story after Wednesday's ruling that his time at Purdue "has come to an end" and he is "excited for what's next."

Kaufman-Renn made the All-Big Ten first team as a junior during the 2024-25 season. He averaged 11.3 points and 5.2 rebounds per game over the course of his four seasons at Purdue.

A 6'3", 190-pound prospect out of McEachern High School in Georgia, Lumpkin is the latest recruiting win for Alabama head coach Nate Oats. The Crimson Tide's 2026 recruiting class was ranked sixth in 247Sports' composite , headlined by prospects Qayden Samuels and Jaxon Richardson.

247Sports director of scouting Adam Finkelstein described Lumpkin as a "big guard with long arms (6-foot-8 wingspan), a nose for the ball, and a budding versatile skill set." "Lumpkin is a true combo-guard, with real on/off ball versatility," Finkelstein stated. "He may ultimately be capable of evolving into a big-lead guard, or full-time initiator (2:1 assist-to-turnover ratio), but isn't quite that yet. He plays at his own pace, but is smoother and craftier than he is naturally explosive with his first step."

Under Oats' direction, the Crimson Tide have made it to at least the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Tournament in each of the last four years. Alabama has long been known as a football school, but it's clear that the basketball program has also established itself as a national powerhouse.

Landing Lumpkin is a strong sign that the Crimson Tide will maintain their status as national championship contenders for years to come.

articles.title: New Lakers Rumors Reveal Heat Exec Hired as Rob Pelinka's Assistant GM Ahead of NBA Season
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers reportedly made an addition to the team's front office on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers reportedly made an addition to the team's front office on Wednesday.

According to ESPN's Shams Charania , the Lakers hired former Miami Heat vice president of player personnel Eric Amsler as an assistant general manager under president of basketball operations Rob Pelinka.

Amsler previously spent over 22 years with the Heat organization, operating in several roles.

After graduating from Dickinson College in 1999, he first joined Miami as an intern ahead of the 2004-05 season.

Amsler eventually served as the team's scouting and information coordinator from 2005-07 before operating as a scouting and player personnel coordinator from 2007-14.

He was later promoted to director of scouting operations for the Heat in 2015, remaining in the position for three years.

Amsler then joined the front office of the Sioux Falls Skyforce, Miami's G League affiliate, in 2018 and remained with the squad until 2023.

He returned to the Heat organization that year, becoming their vice president of player personnel and remaining in the role before heading to the Lakers.

Pat Riley, Miami's team president, previously brought up Amsler when praising the team's ability to identify young talent in Oct. 2020.

"I really want to thank Eric Amsler, Chet Kammerer and Adam Simon, our scouting staff, all those guys that go out and search down, hunt down talent for the Miami Heat," Riley told reporters at the time. "I take very little credit for that. I just want to thank them so much for being able to fill up the cupboard with young talent."

Amsler is the latest addition to the Lakers' front office, as they previously hired Rohan Ramadas as an assistant general manager in May. Ramadas was the New Orleans Pelicans' vice president of strategy and operations before joining Los Angeles.

The Lakers will look to continue building around Luka Dončić as they attempt to make a fifth consecutive playoff appearance next season.

articles.title: Thunder rumors: Cason Wallace could command a $33 million annual salary, per NBA insider
articles.summary: After Oklahoma City Thunder GM Sam Presti made some difficult decisions in order to get from under the dreaded second apron, many wonder how he’ll be approac...
articles.body:
After Oklahoma City Thunder GM Sam Presti made some difficult decisions in order to get from under the dreaded second apron, many wonder how he'll be approaching Cason Wallace 's looming contract extension ahead of the October 19 deadline. Presti moved on from three Thunder veterans this summer — Isaiah Joe , Aaron Wiggins , and Lu Dort. This paves a way toward re-signing Wallace, as many anticipate will be Oklahoma City's latest contract ahead of the upcoming season.

Presti re-signed Thunder starting center Isaiah Hartenstein to a three-year, $75 million extension this summer, which cemented Oklahoma City's frontcourt, featuring All-Star Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams for the foreseeable future. For some, Hartenstein's new deal is a bargain compared to what he could have earned in the open market.

However, will Wallace, a vital piece to the Thunder's backcourt, especially after Dort's departure, be willing to take a similar pay cut for a team competing for its second championship in three seasons?

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

After talking with 10-15 NBA front office members asked to rank Wallace in comparision to members of his 2023 draft class who have yet to reach their first contract extension, including Orlando Magic 's Anthony Black , and Golden State Warriors ' Brandin Podziemski , Wallace was unanimously deemed most likely to receive the highest pay raise of the three, according to NBA insider Zach Lowe.

"It probably wouldn't surprise you that Cason Wallac was universally the No.1 rated player of these three by rival front office people," Lowe said. "I did not text anyone with these teams. I didn't want to put them in that position. Generally, guesses for his annual average salary and what would be fair were 25 on the low end and 33 on the high end."

For Thunder's Cason Wallace 's services, north of $25 million isn't as absurd as some would think, as an investment for what the fourth-year guard is projected to become in Oklahoma City. Wallace, 22, has shown expotential growth over the years from a 3-and-D prospect to one of the better on-ball defenders in the NBA.

While his scoring much to be desired, averaging a career-best 8.4 points last season for a guard who could be on the cusp of making over $25 million in the near future, that's not why the Thunder value his production. Wallace's defense shines the brightest. Staying in front of opposing team's best guards, Cason proved his worth while connecting on 37.4% of his 3-point attempts throughout his first three years in Oklahoma City.

He made his first All-Defensive Team last season while finishing second to Detroit Pistons ' Ausar Thompson as the 2026 steals champion. Wallace led the NBA in total steals with 150 swipes throughout the 2025-26 season and is in position to lock down a vital role alongside two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in the Thunder's starting lineup in 2026-27.

articles.title: Australia será el rival de España en los cuartos de final del Mundial
articles.standfirst: Ganó a Italia en un partido en el que brilló Isobel Borlase y en el que Italia remontó 26 puntos
articles.summary: Ganó a Italia en un partido en el que brilló Isobel Borlase y en el que Italia remontó 26 puntos
articles.body: Es lo que tiene este Mundial tan atípico. Hasta última hora de este miércoles España no conoció al que será su rival en los cuartos que se tienen que jugar menos de 24 horas después. Y será Australia el equipo que se mida a las de Miguel Méndez buscando un lugar en la lucha por las medallas. Las australianas, a pesar de contar con dos bajas muy importantes, que lo serán también contra España, empezó a ganar el partido desde el inicio y llegó a dominar hasta por 26 (38-64), gracias al partido de Isobel Borlase que en el descanso llevaba 23 puntos y al final del choque acabó con 30. Las italianas reaccionaron al final y a punto estuvieron de dar la vuelta al partido cuando en una espectacular remontada lograron igualar el partido a 77 a falta de 1:46 para el final. Una canasta de Aokuso puso de nuevo por delante a las oceánicas (77-79). Sobre la bocina Pasa lanzó para empatar, pero no entró y Australia se llevó el triunfo, 80-82. El choque no lo jugó Alanna Smith, lesionada y de la que su selección confirmó que ya no jugará más en el Mundial. Y a los cuatro minutos de partido, Ezi Magbegor también se lesionó en una jugada fortuita que tiene muy mala pinta. Ninguna de las dos jugadoras estará este jueves contra España a partir de las 20.45 en el que será el último de los partidos de cuartos de final. Smith es una jugadora que promedia 10 puntos y 8 rebotes en el torneo mientras que Magbegor está firmando 15,7 puntos y 6,3 rebotes por partido.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Discusses Angel Reese Relationship, What She Admires About WNBA Star's Game
articles.summary: Even though Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese are best known for their on-court rivalry that dates back to college, there is a respect between the two stars as they have teamed up on Team USA in the FIBA World Cup.
articles.body:
Even though Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese are best known for their on-court rivalry that dates back to college, there is a respect between the two stars as they have teamed up on Team USA in the FIBA World Cup.

Speaking to Doug Feinberg of the Associated Press, Clark opened up about her relationship with Reese by explaining what she admires about her game:

"We're both fiery, fiery competitors and we want to win and it's one of the things I really admire about her game. She's competitive and she has a tremendous motor, like she has one of the best motors in the league. She works just as hard as anybody on the court. So, it's been fun to to be able to play with her."
